item.title: Chasing Achievement Isn’t Enough: What Harvard Tells Us About Contentment |104
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

Have you ever achieved something you thought would make you happy… only to feel a hollow kind of disappointment instead? In this solo episode, I dig into new Harvard research on how mind-wandering and overthinking steal joy, and why chasing big goals doesn’t necessarily bring peace. We’ll explore personal stories, psychological traps, and small shifts that actually move the needle — not just on success, but on contentment.

Support the show: https://www.buzzsprout.com/2302168/support

Key Takeaways:
 • Happiness isn’t a finish line you cross with a goal — often, the chasing steals the joy.
 • Your mind wandering to what could be is a huge thief of contentment.
 • Metrics (followers, achievements) can feel empty unless anchored in meaning.
 • Tiny rituals + gratitude + noticing small wins help you feel grounded now, not later.

Resources & References:
 • Harvard study on mind wandering & well-being (Author, Year)
 • Article in Emotion (2024) on evaluative overthinking

item.title: Why Your Happiness Always Returns to Baseline (and How to Raise It) | 103
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

In 1978, researchers compared two groups you’d never expect: lottery winners and accident victims who had become paraplegic. The results shocked the world.

Within a year, both groups had returned to nearly the same level of happiness as before.

This is the science of hedonic adaptation — our brain’s tendency to normalize no matter what happens. Winning millions. Losing everything. We always come back to baseline.

But here’s the hopeful part: your baseline isn’t fixed. You can raise it.

In this episode, I break down:
 • The famous “lottery vs. paraplegic” study on baseline happiness.
 • Why we imagine extremes in the future (arrival fallacy).
 • Four science-backed ways to elevate your baseline happiness: gratitude, relationships, purposeful work, and meditation.
 • How to frame the future realistically so you’re no longer disappointed by extremes.

🎧 Whether you’re chasing big goals or recovering from setbacks, this episode will show you how to live at a higher baseline.

item.title: I Published 100 Podcasts at 18: I Learned This | 100
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

Hitting 100 episodes feels wild. I started The Grateful Podcast as a 16-year-old kid in France with nothing but curiosity and a mic. Today I’m looking back at the biggest lessons from this journey—the ones that reshaped how I think, how I live, and what I want to build going forward.

Key Discussion Points
• Gratitude rewires your brain for joy
• Do the hard thing, not busywork
• Beliefs put ceilings on our potential
• Non-attachment means embracing all of life
• Anxiety is an engine light, not the problem
• Fame and money don’t equal fulfillment
• Balancing gratitude with ambition daily

This is a thank-you episode—for every single person who has tuned in, shared an episode, or just reminded me why I keep going. I’m nowhere near done.

At 31, David Meltzer had everything people chase. Money. Fame. The dream wife. And still, he was empty. In this episode we dig into how losing it all led him to gratitude, and why gratitude is way more than just saying “thanks.” If you’ve ever wondered why success can feel hollow, or how to actually build a life that feels full, this one’s for you.

item.title: 60% of Young Adults Are Lost: 7 Ways to Not Be One of Them | 98
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

Did you know that 60% of young adults say their lives feel purposeless—and half say it’s harming their mental health?
That’s from Harvard’s On Edge report. But purpose isn’t just some fluffy idea—it’s essential. Without it, rates of anxiety and depression nearly double.

In this episode, I share 7 psychology-backed ways to create more meaning in your life—starting today.

These are not hacks or quick fixes. They’re sustainable practices rooted in psychology and real human connection.

✨ Here’s what you’ll learn:
1.Why deep relationships literally keep you alive
2.How serving others sparks a “helper’s high” in your brain
3.How to rewrite your life story into one of meaning
4.Why goals that go beyond yourself create lasting motivation
5.The secret power of active listening & mentorship
6.How to explore your identity & values without getting stuck
7.Why transcendent practices (like meditation or nature) shift everything

🔑 Key Stat: 58% of young adults lack meaning—don’t be one of them. Start with one practice today, and watch your purpose grow.

item.title: Why Your Fitness Goals Are Destroying Your Health with Jim Laird | 97
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

Most people think getting healthy means training harder, eating cleaner, and pushing further. Jim Laird disagrees.

After 25+ years coaching everyone from NFL pros to everyday people, Jim’s learned that chasing extreme performance often destroys long-term health. In this episode, he shares the 5 fundamentals that can completely reset your energy, sleep, and mood — without the burnout cycle.

We cover:

  • Why most fitness advice fails
  • The “indoor zoo” effect destroying human health
  • Health vs. performance (and why you don’t need to train like a pro athlete)
  • The role of play in building lifelong physical resilience
  • How connection + nature can replace 90% of what people chase in gyms and supplements

If you feel stuck, burnt out, or like you’ve “tried everything” — this episode will change how you think about health forever.

item.title: 7 Proven Ways To Feel MORE Joy | 96
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

Most people think joy is something that happens to you when life is perfect. They wait for the “aha” moment, the dream job, the perfect relationship — and then wonder why they still feel empty when it arrives. In this solo episode, 96, of The Grateful Podcast, Jack shares why joy isn’t a lucky accident, but a skill you can train — just like learning an instrument or building muscle.

Backed by science and real-life stories, Jack breaks down 7 powerful, proven habits you can start today to rewire your brain for joy:
•Train your brain to notice micro moments
•Move your body in ways you love
•Savor like a scientist
•Do something kind anonymously
•Create more than you consume
•Connect deeply — even briefly
•Practice joy on a delay

If you’ve been feeling burnt out, stuck, or like happiness keeps slipping away, this episode will give you both the mindset shift and the actionable steps to make joy show up more often in your life — without chasing it.

Most people think joy is something that happens to you when life is perfect. They wait for the “aha” moment, the dream job, the perfect relationship — and then wonder why they still feel empty when it arrives. In this solo episode, 96, of The Grateful Podcast, Jack shares why joy isn’t a lucky accident, but a skill you can train — just like learning an instrument or building muscle.

Backed by science and real-life stories, Jack breaks down 7 powerful, proven habits you can start today to rewire your brain for joy:
•Train your brain to notice micro moments
•Move your body in ways you love
•Savor like a scientist
•Do something kind anonymously
•Create more than you consume
•Connect deeply — even briefly
•Practice joy on a delay

If you’ve been feeling burnt out, stuck, or like happiness keeps slipping away, this episode will give you both the mindset shift and the actionable steps to make joy show up more often in your life — without chasing it.

item.title: You Are the Cause of Your Problems and That’s Good with Jeremy Grater | 95
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

What if the worst thing that ever happened to you… was actually the beginning of everything good?

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 95
Guesting Jeremy Grater

In this powerful episode of The Grateful Podcast, Jack Wagoner sits down with Jeremy Grater—longtime podcaster, father, and co-founder of the newly rebranded BroBots, a podcast on AI and mental health. Jeremy shares how a random knee injury transformed his life, how biking taught him presence, and how purpose is not a job title but a way of being.

They dive into:
 • Why you are the cause AND the solution to your problems
 • The surprising rise of AI as a therapist substitute
 • The truth about purpose, ambition, and family
 • How gratitude can drive ambition, not diminish it
 • Why Jeremy left status and comfort behind to chase real peace
 • The link between meditation, neuroscience, and emotional resilience
 • The cost of chasing the wrong definition of success
 • The hidden loneliness of growth and how to combat it

item.title: How To Wake Up Joyful Every Day | 94
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

Support The Grateful Podcast: https://www.buzzsprout.com/2302168/support

You’ve been taught your whole life that joy comes after success.

Get the job → feel proud.
Hit six figures → feel fulfilled.
Hit the goal → finally feel enough.

But what if that formula is broken?

In this solo episode, 18-year-old podcast host Jack Wagoner breaks down the real reason so many people feel lost, disconnected, and burnt out—even when they’re doing everything “right.”

You’ll learn:
 • Why your entire reward system is rigged against your joy
 • How to stop outsourcing your peace to a future version of yourself
 • The surprising Buddhist insight that will change how you think about time
 • Why ambition without gratitude guarantees emptiness
 • How to wake up excited—even if nothing changes externally

This episode will reprogram the way you think about success, happiness, and identity. If you’re stuck in the cycle of chasing and still don’t feel “there,” this is the conversation you need.

Chapters:
00:00 Embracing Gratitude and Joy

item.title: Why Achievement Is NOT Success with James Brackin IV | 93
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

James Brackin started coaching people twice his age at 17. At 21, he’s hosted over 300 episodes of the You Can Too Podcast and built a life completely on his own terms — without college, without a corporate job, and without waiting for permission.

In episode 93 of The Grateful Podcast, we go deep on what it really takes to live with intention in your early 20s — from investing in yourself with money you don’t have, to navigating self-doubt, to redefining success outside of social expectations.

We talk about:
 • The Be-Do-Have mindset
 • Escaping the trap of chasing outcomes
 • Why most people are just not “f*cking around enough to find out”
 • How to build credibility as a young creator
 • Why true success is internal, not external

Whether you’re 18 or 38, this conversation will challenge the way you think about ambition, balance, and what it means to live a life worth living.

item.title: How Trying Too Hard Is RUINING Your Success | 92
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

Why Trying Harder Isn’t Always the Answer

In this solo episode of The Grateful Podcast, Jack Wagoner flips the hustle narrative on its head.

You’re doing everything right. You care more than most. You push harder than anyone you know. So… why isn’t it working?

Enter: The Backwards Law.

Jack dives deep into the paradox that the more we chase success, happiness, peace, or achievement—the more resistance we create. From his days grinding for a baseball dream to launching a top 2.5% podcast, Jack shares why letting go might just be the secret weapon nobody talks about.

This episode explores:
• The truth behind why trying too hard creates failure
• The difference between surrender and giving up
• Why desperation lowers your perceived value
• How to move from panic to peace without losing your ambition
• A practical framework for chasing goals without losing yourself
• A vulnerable look into Jack’s recent internal battles and breakthroughs

Whether you’re chasing success, building a dream, or just trying to breathe again—this episode is your invitation to ease up, trust more, and fall back in love with the process.

item.title: The Hidden Crisis Behind Anxiety and Disconnection with Trey Tucker | 91
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 91
Guesting Trey Tucker

Support the show: https://www.buzzsprout.com/2302168/support

Why are so many young people, especially men, feeling lost, anxious, and disconnected?

In this powerful episode of The Grateful Podcast, I sit down with therapist Trey Tucker (aka @ruggedcounseling) to unpack the quiet crisis in masculinity and mental health.

We dive deep into:
 • The real reason anxiety is rising in young men
 • Why the gym, hustle, and self-help culture often mask emotional pain
 • How to find your calling in a world full of noise
 • The difference between happiness, joy, and fulfillment
 • And why being still might be the bravest thing you do

If you’ve ever felt numb, directionless, or just unsure of what it means to be a man today—this conversation is for you.

Trey’s wisdom will hit you in the gut and heal you at the same time.

Chapters:
0:00 Intro – Why young men are confused  
3:42 Anxiety is a messenger, not a malfunction  
8:19 The trap of instant solutions  
13:06 Stop chasing happiness — chase this instead  
17:30 How to get unstuck  
22:50 3 reasons anxiety is rising today  
28:40 What anxiety really wants you to do  
33:45 Are you addicted to productivity?  
38:10 Gym culture, discipline & emotional avoidance  
44:20 Why calling is the antidote to numbness  
49:00 Rethinking masculinity  
52:35 What Trey would say to every young man  
56:00 Gratitude + ambition = fulfillment  
59:25 Healing is remembering who you are

item.title: How to Live to 120 (and Love Every Minute of It) with Matt Zenith Project | 90
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

What if your 20s weren’t for burning out… but for biohacking your way to 120?

Support the show: https://www.buzzsprout.com/2302168/support

In this mind-expanding episode of The Grateful Podcast, I sit down with Matt, founder of Zenith Health, Dartmouth-trained biomedical engineer, and longevity strategist, to explore how young people can optimize for a longer, more fulfilling life — starting right now.

We talk:
• The REAL science behind living to 120+
• Why VO2 max and HRV matter more than you think
• How to build a morning routine like a bioengineer
• Why purpose might be the most important longevity tool
• The truth about cold plunges, creatine, and supplements

Whether you’re 18 or 80, this episode will make you rethink everything about aging, energy, and what’s possible for your future.

item.title: Why You're Setting Goals WRONG (and how to fix it) | 89
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

You’ve hit your goals—but why does it still feel like something’s missing?

In this solo episode, Jack Wagoner flips the script on traditional goal setting and reveals why chasing external achievements will never bring the fulfillment you’re looking for. From his own story of getting into Northeastern to reaching 10K podcast downloads, Jack shares the harsh truth: our goals aren’t broken—our relationship with them is.

This episode explores:
 • Why outcomes never lead to lasting peace
 • How to reverse-engineer your life based on how you want to feel
 • The “Be → Do → Have” model that actually works
 • How to escape the empty high of constant achievement
 • A practical challenge to help you redefine your goals today

Whether you’re chasing success, growth, or clarity—this episode will help you ground your ambition in presence, alignment, and lasting fulfillment.

item.title: Why Achieving More is NOT The Answer with Jess Prudhomme | 88
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner

Episode 88

Guesting Jess Prudhomme

At 35, Jess Prudhomme had checked every box: corporate success, a polished identity, a picture-perfect marriage. But beneath the surface was a quiet ache — the haunting question, “Is this really me?”

In this raw and powerful conversation, Jess shares how her greatest detours — divorce, quitting her job, walking away from security — were not breakdowns, but breakthroughs. Together, we explore:

  • Letting go of identities that no longer fit


  • Why ambition can be a mask for fear


  • How to follow a gut feeling without a plan


  • Why success is nothing without alignment


  • How to trust yourself when everything feels uncertain

item.title: Why Adversity IS The Path To Success with Joshua Dean Church | 87
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 87
Guesting Joshua Dean Church

Born with a collapsed lung and told he’d never be an athlete, Joshua Dean Church defied the odds—completing an Ironman and sending the finish line photo to the doctor who once doubted him. A Forbes 30 Under 30 entrepreneur, Josh built a $20M company in three years, only to shut it down when it no longer aligned with his purpose.

In this deep, soulful, and fiercely honest episode, Josh shares:
 • How adversity isn’t in the way—it becomes the way
 • Why leading others starts with leading yourself
 • The 5 pillars of modern leadership
 • His journey from black sheep to heart-centered leader
 • The dance between faith, intuition, and ambition
 • What “living what you rap about” really means

We talk journaling, mental toughness, spiritual growth, and how to find the next step when you feel completely lost.

36:55 The Power of Gratitude and Ambition

item.title: The Hard Truth About Betting On Myself at 18 | 86
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 86

Support the show: https://www.buzzsprout.com/2302168/support

In this solo episode, I open up about what it’s really like to choose the long game at 18 years old—pursuing my podcast, building a climbing clothing brand, and saying no to a typical summer job.

I talk about comparison traps, jealousy, creative isolation, and how I’ve found freedom by building a life that looks different—and loving it anyway. I also share the daily habits that make me more productive (even if they look “unproductive”), and why prioritizing joy, nature, and self-reflection has made all the difference.

Whether you’re carving your own path, chasing something unconventional, or just trying to stay motivated—this one’s for you.

⚡ Plus, I share my personal challenge: hitting 100,000 podcast downloads before I start college at Northeastern on August 31st.

item.title: The Psychology Behind Astrology with Carmen Turner Schott | 85
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 85
Guesting Carmen Turner Schott

In this episode of The Grateful Podcast, I sit down with Carmen Turner Schott, a licensed clinical social worker, trauma therapist, and professional astrologer who has worked for over 25 years in the U.S. Air Force. Together, we explore the intersection of astrology and psychology, challenging assumptions and expanding perspectives.

Initially skeptical, I came into this conversation with questions—and I left with new insight into how astrology might serve as a tool for self-awareness, healing, and transformation.

We dive into:
•How Carmen bridges ancient astrology with modern trauma therapy
•The surprising origins of astrology in medicine and religion
•Why full birth charts go deeper than horoscopes or memes
•Real stories of healing, intuition, and transformation
•Ethical concerns and scientific research in astrology
•Whether astrology can complement or surpass traditional therapy
•The role of free will vs. destiny in astrological interpretation

If you’re a skeptic, a believer, or just curious—this conversation will challenge you to look at astrology in a whole new light.

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 85
Guesting Carmen Turner Schott

In this episode of The Grateful Podcast, I sit down with Carmen Turner Schott, a licensed clinical social worker, trauma therapist, and professional astrologer who has worked for over 25 years in the U.S. Air Force. Together, we explore the intersection of astrology and psychology, challenging assumptions and expanding perspectives.

Initially skeptical, I came into this conversation with questions—and I left with new insight into how astrology might serve as a tool for self-awareness, healing, and transformation.

We dive into:
•How Carmen bridges ancient astrology with modern trauma therapy
•The surprising origins of astrology in medicine and religion
•Why full birth charts go deeper than horoscopes or memes
•Real stories of healing, intuition, and transformation
•Ethical concerns and scientific research in astrology
•Whether astrology can complement or surpass traditional therapy
•The role of free will vs. destiny in astrological interpretation

If you’re a skeptic, a believer, or just curious—this conversation will challenge you to look at astrology in a whole new light.

item.title: How Travel and Language Rewired His Brain for Gratitude with Lachie Colledge | 84
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 84
Guesting Lachie Colledge

What if the key to living a truly grateful life was hidden in a foreign language—or in a 7-year-old street kid’s smile?

Today’s guest is Lachie Colledge, a medical student who left behind textbooks to travel the world in search of something deeper. From monasteries in Myanmar to roadside reflections in Norway, Lachie’s story is a masterclass in mindfulness, purpose, and finding gratitude in the most unexpected places.

In this conversation, we explore:
 • What “gratitude” really means (and why most of us are doing it wrong)
 • Why a single French word changed Lachie’s life
 • How a moment in India with a street kid flipped his understanding of generosity
 • The link between reconnaissance, gratitude, and ambition
 • Why meditation isn’t just calming—it’s painful, raw, and transformational
 • How to find joy without changing your life—just your awareness

If you’ve ever struggled to balance gratitude with ambition… this episode is for you.

Takeaways:
Gratitude is about being intentional and present.
Decisions can be made through intuition and logic.
Language encodes wisdom and life lessons.
Understanding pain leads to compassion for others.
Meditation helps in self-discovery and clarity.
We are interconnected and dependent on others.
Gratitude can drive ambition and purpose.
Small acts of kindness hold significant value.
Travel teaches profound lessons about generosity.
Our journey is shaped by those who support us.

item.title: Does Ambition Cost Happiness? | 83
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 83
Solo Episode

In this episode, Jack Wagoner explores the concept of sacrifice and its relationship to fulfillment and success. He reflects on the inherent struggle between ambition and gratitude, sharing personal anecdotes and insights from successful figures like Alex Hormozi. The conversation delves into the challenges of balancing personal desires with the sacrifices required to achieve them, ultimately emphasizing the importance of finding contentment in the present while pursuing future goals.

Takeaways:
We are inherently bad at sacrifice.
Everything has a price, especially time.
Fulfillment is often the finish line we chase.
Success is supposed to bring happiness, but we sacrifice happiness for success.
Some people find satisfaction in simpler lives.
Gratitude helps lessen the pain of sacrifice.
We can't have everything; embracing sacrifices is key.
The duality of gratitude and ambition is ever-shifting.
Finding balance between inward peace and outward success is challenging.
Reflection is essential for growth and understanding.

item.title: Travel Can't Really Change You | 82
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 82
Solo Episode

In this episode, Jack Wagoner shares his experiences on his trip out west, reflecting on the beauty of nature and the expectations we set for personal growth during such journeys. He emphasizes the importance of soaking in experiences without the pressure of achieving inner peace or change, advocating for patience and the understanding that personal growth is a gradual process. Jack also discusses the significance of desires and how they can impact our sense of control in life, concluding with a reminder to appreciate the present moment.

Takeaways:
Expecting change from external experiences can be misleading.
Personal growth requires patience and cannot be rushed.
Setting unrealistic goals can limit your experience.
Enjoy experiences for their own sake, not for what they might change within you.
Accumulation of experiences leads to deeper change.
Fictional stories can provide valuable life lessons.
Desires can create a sense of control or victimhood in life.
Letting go of unattainable desires can bring peace.
Gratitude enhances the experience of life.

item.title: Curiosity Is Your Superpower — Jon Bassford on Purpose, Innovation & Inner Peace | 81
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 81
Guest: Jon Bassford

What if your greatest leadership strength wasn’t authority, experience, or intelligence—but curiosity?

In this episode of The Grateful Podcast, Jack Wagoner sits down with Jon Bassford—entrepreneur, operations strategist, TEDx speaker, and author of The Curious Leader—to explore how asking better questions can unlock innovation, deepen self-understanding, and transform not just your team, but your life.

They dive into the chaos and beauty of curiosity: how it can feel overwhelming, how it can set you free, and how it might just be the missing piece in both solopreneurship and scaling businesses alike. If you’ve ever felt pulled in too many directions, questioned your path, or sensed that there’s more to life than just “doing the job”—this episode is for you.

⸻

🎯 Topics Covered:
 • Why curiosity is the ultimate superpower
 • The danger of chasing the wrong outcomes
 • How to reframe purpose as a verb, not a destination
 • Surface-level curiosity vs. deep, wonder-driven exploration
 • The power of reflection, meditation, and self-inquiry
 • Building a life from the inside out (and staying sane while doing it)
 • Scaling as a solopreneur and knowing when to let go
 • How gratitude and ambition create a meaningful, sustainable life

item.title: Finding Opportunity Between Expectation and Reality | 80
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 80

In this solo episode, Jack Wagoner reflects on his recent experiences while traveling in Boulder, Colorado. He discusses the importance of embracing the journey, being present in the moment, and learning through observation. Jack contrasts the pleasure of expectation with the reality of experiences, emphasizing the need to adapt and find joy in the present rather than clinging to preconceived notions. Through his reflections, he shares insights on personal growth, gratitude, and the beauty of life's unpredictability.

Takeaways:
Go with the flow of whatever happens.
Life has a plan for you.
We have to be open to change and embrace it.
True joy comes from being present.
We learn so much through observation.
Productivity is all about what you're optimizing for.
The pleasure of expectation versus the pleasure of just actually being here.
Ride the wave of life where it's taking you.
This has been the least productive period of my life.
Stay grateful. Love you.

item.title: The Technology That Centers You with Steven Schrembeck | 79
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 79
Guesting Stephen Schrembeck

What if the next frontier of human connection isn’t less tech—but better tech?

In this mind-opening episode of The Grateful Podcast, Jack Wagoner sits down with Stephen Schrembeck, founder of Impossible Labs, to explore how we can redesign technology to deepen presence, amplify our humanity, and support mental well-being.

Stephen shares how his personal experience with ADHD and a lifetime of reflection sparked a movement to reimagine how we use tech—from minimalist wearable tools like Cognizant Threads to powerful mental models for focus, meditation, and emotional resilience. They dive deep into the philosophy of building from curiosity, the power of silence, dopamine rebalancing, and how to stay grounded while pursuing meaningful, ambitious goals.

Whether you’re an entrepreneur, thinker, creative, or someone feeling overstimulated by modern life—this episode is a must-listen.

⸻

🎯 What We Cover:
 • Why “less tech” isn’t the solution—but better tech is
 • How Stephen manages ADHD without distraction
 • The story behind Impossible Labs and designing for the edge
 • Tools for extending focus, attention, and presence
 • How meditation reshaped his mind (and why it matters more than meds)
 • Why boredom is actually the antidote to overstimulation
 • The chair test: can you sit in silence for 5 minutes?
 • How to create while staying unburdened by outcome
 • The duality of ambition and stillness—and how to hold both

⸻

item.title: I Am Leaving For Three Weeks | 78
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 78

In this raw and reflective solo episode, Jack Wagoner records a late-night message just hours before leaving on a cross-country road trip—and only days after graduating high school.

It’s a moment suspended in time: everything feels the same, and yet everything is about to change. From letting go of childhood and buzzing off his beloved curls, to saying goodbye to the people who shaped him, Jack opens up about the beauty and sadness of transition, the fleeting feeling of big milestones, and what it means to truly trust life.

⸻

🎯 Topics Covered:
 • Why reaching your biggest goals can feel… weird
 • The grief of growing up and moving on
 • Family, time, and the bittersweet nature of change
 • Letting go of identity (even the hair you loved)
 • How to hold gratitude and excitement at once
 • Learning to trust the unknown
 • Reflections on purpose, presence, and becoming

In this raw and reflective solo episode, Jack Wagoner records a late-night message just hours before leaving on a cross-country road trip—and only days after graduating high school.

It’s a moment suspended in time: everything feels the same, and yet everything is about to change. From letting go of childhood and buzzing off his beloved curls, to saying goodbye to the people who shaped him, Jack opens up about the beauty and sadness of transition, the fleeting feeling of big milestones, and what it means to truly trust life.

⸻

🎯 Topics Covered:
 • Why reaching your biggest goals can feel… weird
 • The grief of growing up and moving on
 • Family, time, and the bittersweet nature of change
 • Letting go of identity (even the hair you loved)
 • How to hold gratitude and excitement at once
 • Learning to trust the unknown
 • Reflections on purpose, presence, and becoming

item.title: Philosophy in the Age of Algorithms – Justin Smith Ruiu on Truth, Tech & the Self | 77
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 77
Guesting Professor Justin Smith Ruiu

In this mind-expanding episode of The Grateful Podcast, Jack Wagoner sits down with philosopher and historian of ideas Justin E.H. Smith—author of The Internet Is Not What You Think It Is and creator of The Hinternet Substack.

Together, they dive into:
 • Why philosophy has been exiled from everyday life
 • How the internet distorts identity and consciousness
 • Whether AI can replicate human thought
 • What we lose when we let machines think for us
 • How to stay human in an increasingly algorithmic world

If you’re interested in technology, truth, or what it means to be human, this is an episode you won’t want to miss.

item.title: Graduation, Stoicism & the Power of Chosen Struggle | 76
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 76
Monday Solo Episode

In this solo episode of The Grateful Podcast, Jack Wagoner shares a raw, late-night reflection on graduating high school and the whirlwind of emotions that come with it. From saying goodbye to lifelong friends to realizing that some relationships are meant to last—and some aren’t—Jack opens up about what it means to move forward.

He also shares a powerful insight from Stoicism: how chosen suffering prepares us for life’s unchosen hardships. This episode explores Jack’s evolving relationship with work, purpose, and the importance of consistency, even when life is full and energy is low. If you’re in a transitional season, this honest episode will speak directly to you.

🎓 Topics covered:
 • Letting go of people and places as life changes
 • Why some relationships are seasonal—and why that’s okay
 • The discipline of doing hard things consistently
 • What Stoicism teaches about inner peace
 • How podcasting cultivates daily gratitude
 • Why contribution matters more than perfection

item.title: Rebuild Your Life From The Inside Out with Steve Gamlin | 75
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 75
Guesting Steve Gamlin

Most people build their dreams based on someone else’s definition of success.
In this powerful and heartfelt episode of The Grateful Podcast, Jack Wagoner sits down with speaker, author, and visualization coach Steve Gamlin—a man who rebuilt his life from rock bottom and now teaches others how to see and live a life that aligns with their values.

Steve shares how he went from debt, divorce, and depression to joy, gratitude, and purpose—and how you can do it too. Whether you’ve made a vision board or feel stuck between who you are and who you want to be, this episode offers practical wisdom, deep stories, and a whole lot of humanity.

🎯 What We Cover:
•Why most people’s goals are built on ego, not alignment
•The 8 areas of life you should visualize (not just money)
•How to make vision boards that actually work
•Balancing ambition with gratitude
•How to keep going after grief and loss
•The ripple effect of small acts of kindness
•How to reframe negative thoughts with humor and humanity
•Why you’re planting either seeds or weeds every day

Website: https://stevegamlin.com/about/
LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/stevegamlin/
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/stevegamlin/

item.title: Escaping Default: How to Live a Life You Love with Dr. Wendy O’Connor | 74
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 74 
Guesting Dr. Wendy O'Connor

In this episode of The Grateful Podcast, Jack Wagoner sits down with licensed therapist and life strategist Dr. Wendy O’Connor to talk about default settings, rewiring your mind, and reclaiming your future. If you feel like you’re just checking boxes, stuck in survival mode, or disconnected from your purpose—this is the episode for you.

With over 20 years of experience in neuroscience, clinical psychology, and personal growth, Dr. Wendy breaks down how to overcome conditioning, tune into your inner voice, and design a life that actually lights you up.

🎯 Topics Covered:
•The “default life” trap (and how to break out)
•What “languishing” really means
•Why your brain is wired to keep you stuck
•How to tune out the noise and find your inner voice
•The science and soul of designing a life that feels like YOU
•When to say yes, and when to say NO
•The myth of long-term goals (and what to do instead)

Her website: https://www.drwendyoconnor.com/

item.title: Living Inside Out: How I am Finding Peace | 73
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 73

In this deeply personal solo episode, I reflect on the whirlwind of my final week of high school—and the mindset shift that’s changing my life. From quitting a new job after one sale, to letting go of external pressure and choosing alignment, this is an unfiltered look at what it means to live from the inside out.

I share how I'm learning to say no with confidence, why space in your schedule matters, and how rereading Siddhartha helped me return to my core philosophy of joy, meaning, and mindful ambition.

If you’re in a season of transition, growth, or simply trying to find your way, this episode will resonate.

🎙️ Topics We Cover:
 • Letting go of opportunities that look good on paper
 • How to listen to your internal compass
 • Why saying no is a superpower
 • Reconnecting with joy and authenticity
 • Life after high school: creating your path
 • Rethinking productivity and fulfillment
 • What rereading Siddhartha teaches about inner peace

item.title: The Hidden Cost of Ambition in Love with Talia Bombola | 72
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 72
Guesting Talia Bombola

We’re told to love ourselves and set boundaries—but how do you actually do that?

In this episode of The Grateful Podcast, Jack Wagoner sits down with therapist and confidence specialist Talia Bombola, LMFT to break down what real self-worth looks like, how to build lasting confidence, and what actually defines a healthy relationship.

Whether you’re a high achiever struggling to balance work and love, or someone working through feelings of not-enoughness, this conversation is for you.

Topics we cover:
 • How to rewire your self-worth
 • Why overachievers often burn out in love
 • Confidence vs performative self-assurance
 • What a healthy relationship actually looks like
 • How to balance ambition with intimacy
 • Why “good enough” is sometimes the healthiest goal

item.title: The Secret Breathwork That Unlocks Peace with Jitesh Vaswani | 71
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 71
Guesting Jitesh Vaswani

There’s a quiet war happening inside all of us. Anxiety, overstimulation, endless comparison—especially among Gen Z. In this powerful conversation, Jack Wagoner speaks with Jitesh Vaswani—spiritual teacher, TEDx speaker, and Director of Partnerships & Breathwork Coach at Art of Living with Gurudev Sri Sri Ravi Shankar.

Jitesh breaks down why our generation is facing unprecedented levels of stress, and how SKY Breath Meditation (Sudarshan Kriya Yoga) offers a simple, ancient, and proven practice to reconnect to peace.

We explore:
•The anxiety epidemic in young people
•How breath shapes emotion—and how to use it consciously
•Whether lasting inner peace is really possible
•Meditation myths, and why it’s not just “sitting in silence”
•The difference between conscious and subconscious breath training
•The mission of Art of Living and Jitesh’s spiritual journey

📌 Links Mentioned:
•Jitesh Vaswani Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/jitesh_vaswani
•Art of Living: https://www.artofliving.org
•SKY Breath Meditation Course Info: https://www.artofliving.org/us-en/sky-breath-meditation
•Gurudev Sri Sri Ravi Shankar: https://www.srisriravishankar.org

item.title: Why You Can't Think Your Way Out of Pain | 70
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 70
Solo episode


In this episode, I explore the complexities of pain and emotional distress, emphasizing the importance of embracing emotions rather than suppressing them. I reflect on my journey towards being present, the significance of cultivating a relationship with oneself, and the balance between pursuing future goals and living in the moment. I also invite feedback on the podcast and highlight the organic growth of the show through word of mouth.

Takeaways:
Thinking alone cannot solve emotional pain.
Suppressing emotions leads to worse outcomes.
Embracing emotions can lead to better decision-making.
We often prioritize external validation over self-worth.
A strong relationship with oneself enhances happiness.
Dissatisfaction arises from wanting more than we have.
Balancing future aspirations with present experiences is crucial.
Memories are made in moments of presence.
Feedback is essential for growth and improvement.
The podcast thrives on organic growth through listeners.

item.title: The Art of Living a Magical Life with Daniel Smith | 69
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 69
Guesting Daniel Smith

In this absolutely fantastic conversation with my good friend, poet, and podcaster Daniel Smith, we discussed many things, including:
- The magic of life and how to cultivate it
- How to live your life like a myth and its benefits
- Why explicit personal development content is less effective than fiction
- The difficulties of never being satisfied
- The constant need to do more that both Daniel and I feel
- Each of us have a subjective truth, no objective truth
- There is a massive difference between faith and religion
- How to ground in the "present"
and some other pretty fun things too.

Daniel just left for a trip in which he hopes to find some quiet and peace away from all of the things he pushes himself to do. In the conversation, we talk about this problem of "never enough," and one of the reasons we relate is because it is that very problem that plagues me every day. In fact, next month I will be taking a trip with a similar goal.

Listen to Daniel's newest AMAZING podcast here: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/rage-is-a-tumor-sooo-cut-it-out/id1602998894?i=1000705646751

item.title: How To Lead Yourself to Freedom with Beejal Bilimoria | 68
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 68
Guesting Beejal Bilimoria

What if everything you’re chasing is already inside of you?

In this deep and inspiring episode of The Grateful Podcast, host Jack Wagoner is joined by Beejal Bilimoria—a leadership and identity coach for purpose-driven visionaries. Together, they explore what it really means to lead yourself, heal the nervous system, and live a life of authenticity and expansion.

Beejal shares her personal story of walking away from societal success to embrace deep self-trust and freedom. The conversation moves beyond surface-level mindset work and dives into identity, energy, and embodiment—revealing how safety, surrender, and compassion unlock our truest power.

✨ If you’re navigating self-doubt, imposter syndrome, or simply want to feel more you, this episode is a guide to coming home to yourself.

⸻

item.title: Your Brain Is Lying to You: Why You Don’t Understand Your Decisions | 67
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 67

In this solo episode of The Grateful Podcast, host Jack Wagoner dives deep into why we make the decisions we make, challenging the common belief in human rationality. Drawing from insights in The Undoing Project by Michael Lewis and the groundbreaking research of Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky, Jack questions whether logic and reason are really guiding our behavior—or if we’re missing something deeper.

He shares a vulnerable personal story of choosing between Harvard and Northeastern and explains why trusting his gut feeling led him to a more expansive, fulfilling decision. This episode explores themes of behavioral psychology, intuition, self-examination, and how to build a life based on internal truth rather than external validation.

📚 Referenced:
 • The Undoing Project by Michael Lewis
 • The work of Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky
 • Socratic wisdom: “The unexamined life is not worth living”

🎧 Listen if you’re curious about:
 • Why most of us don’t actually understand our decisions
 • How intuition may be more trustworthy than logic
 • The self-fulfilling prophecy of rationality
 • Letting go of needing to explain your choices to others
 • Designing a life based on inner fulfillment, not prestige

⸻

⏱️ Chapters & Timestamps:

0:00 – The Illusion of Rational Decisions

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 67

In this solo episode of The Grateful Podcast, host Jack Wagoner dives deep into why we make the decisions we make, challenging the common belief in human rationality. Drawing from insights in The Undoing Project by Michael Lewis and the groundbreaking research of Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky, Jack questions whether logic and reason are really guiding our behavior—or if we’re missing something deeper.

He shares a vulnerable personal story of choosing between Harvard and Northeastern and explains why trusting his gut feeling led him to a more expansive, fulfilling decision. This episode explores themes of behavioral psychology, intuition, self-examination, and how to build a life based on internal truth rather than external validation.

📚 Referenced:
 • The Undoing Project by Michael Lewis
 • The work of Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky
 • Socratic wisdom: “The unexamined life is not worth living”

🎧 Listen if you’re curious about:
 • Why most of us don’t actually understand our decisions
 • How intuition may be more trustworthy than logic
 • The self-fulfilling prophecy of rationality
 • Letting go of needing to explain your choices to others
 • Designing a life based on inner fulfillment, not prestige

⸻

item.title: How to Be Ambitious Without Losing Yourself with Tristan Gregoire | 66
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 66
Guest: Tristan Gregoire

What if you could enjoy the present moment and chase your highest potential?

In this episode of The Grateful Podcast, I sit down with Tristan Gregoire, the 23-year-old creator of The Best Self Protocol. We dive deep into the mindset that separates stagnant ambition from sustainable growth. From detaching your happiness from outcomes to making peace with the “now,” this conversation is a masterclass in living skillfully.

🎯 Topics we cover:
• The “trifecta” of spiritual, mental & physical growth
• Why you need a personal compass, not a fixed roadmap
• Balancing gratitude and ambition
• Overcoming the productivity guilt loop
• Wisdom from Socrates, Seneca, Marcus Aurelius, and Naval
• How action—not just introspection—creates clarity

⏱️ Timestamps:
00:00 - Intro to Tristan & The Best Self Protocol
02:00 - Who is your best self?
04:20 - Why process matters more than outcome
06:15 - The paradox of wanting more
09:00 - Choosing between “good enough” and “great”
11:30 - The North Star & your personal compass
13:30 - What Tristan wants most in life
17:30 - Introspection and finding answers within
20:30 - Stoicism, Buddhism & ancient wisdom in modern life
23:00 - What true balance really means
26:30 - Coaching through imperfection and action
29:00 - Lazy ambition vs. real progress
32:00 - Productivity guilt and the happiness equation
36:00 - How to hold ambition and peace at the same time
39:30 - Coaching older clients at 23
44:00 - Age vs. wisdom and intentional growth
48:30 - Why Tristan is a guide, not a guru
50:00 - Fiction vs. nonfiction: where the deepest truths hide
57:00 - Downloading wisdom through stories
1:04:00 - Final thoughts: walk your own path

📌 Connect with Tristan:
• Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/iamtristangregoire/
• Free community is linked in his bio

Key Takeaways
• You are both the artist and the canvas. Your best self is not a finish line—it’s a direction.
• Gratitude doesn’t slow you down—it fuels ambition.
• The rules holding you back are often imaginary.
• You can hold two truths at once: hunger for growth and peace with now.
• True intelligence is measured by your ability to get out of life what you want.
• Books and mentors offer guidance, but the answers are already inside you.
• Wisdom is not about age—it’s about intentional experience.

item.title: I Finally Understand The Magic of Meditation — Susan Piver | 65
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 65
Guesting Susan Piver

What if meditation wasn’t about fixing yourself—but about discovering who you truly are?

In this soul-expanding episode of The Grateful Podcast, Jack Wagoner sits down with Susan Piver, bestselling author, longtime Buddhist practitioner, and founder of the Open Heart Project, the world’s largest virtual mindfulness community. Together, they explore the magic of meditation—not as a productivity tool, but as a profound path toward truth, love, self-compassion, and awakening.

They unravel the paradox of non-attachment in a goal-obsessed culture, reframe suffering through the Buddhist lens of dukkha, and dive into the difference between improving yourself and becoming yourself. If you’ve ever felt like meditation was supposed to calm you down—but instead opened something deeper—you are not alone.

This is not your typical “5 tips to meditate better” kind of conversation. This is a re-enchantment of mindfulness. A reminder that presence is magic. That sitting quietly might be the most rebellious, loving act in a noisy world.

⸻

⏱️ Timestamps:

00:00 – Intro: Who is Susan Piver?
01:38 – “If attachment is suffering, how do we pursue anything?”
06:25 – The Western misunderstanding of meditation
11:04 – Dukkha as dissatisfaction, not suffering
14:12 – What is meditation really asking of us?
18:30 – When data flattens the soul of the practice
22:41 – The danger of meditating with an agenda
27:20 – Can American meditators call themselves Buddhists?
31:18 – What does it mean to live without a self?
35:55 – Meditation as a path to love, not self-improvement
39:02 – “You don’t need to know”: Wisdom in unknowing
42:30 – Final reflections on joy, truth, and the path ahead

🧘‍♀️ Follow Susan Piver
Website: https://susanpiver.com
The Open Heart Project: https://openheartproject.com
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/susan.piver
Books: The Wisdom of a Broken Heart, Start Here Now, The Four Noble Truths of Love

📺 Watch the full episode on YouTube:

Subscribe for more deep conversations with thinkers, seekers, and soulful creators. 🙏

item.title: My Drive Causes My Dissatisfaction— Will College Change It? | 64
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 64

In this episode, I reflect on my upcoming graduation from high school and the changes it will bring to my self-image and identity. I discuss the pressures of perfectionism and achievement that have shaped my life, as well as the duality of comparison in the age of social media. I emphasize the importance of finding balance between ambition and gratitude, and how I am learning to appreciate the present moment while looking forward to the future (The duality of gratitude and ambition).

Takeaways:
I love my life. I truly do.
Graduating high school will affect my self-image.
Perfection and achievement have been core pillars of my identity.
Comparison can be both a blessing and a curse.
I've been craving inner peace and contentment.
Balance in life is not a constant state.
Ambition and gratitude can coexist in different phases.
Living a vivid life experience is what I crave.
Time is a finite resource that I need to manage better.
Sharing this podcast helps it grow.

Chapters:
00:00 Embracing Change and Gratitude
01:16 Reflections on Identity and Achievement
03:51 The Pressure of Comparison
06:10 Finding Balance in Life
09:55 Living Vividly and Immersively
11:26 The Journey Ahead and Future Aspirations

item.title: Inside The Mind of True Happiness— Gratitude | 61
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

Inside the Grateful Mind | Jack Wagoner

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner 
Episode 61

In this episode of The Grateful Podcast,  I dive deep into the science of gratitude — and how it can literally rewire your brain for greater happiness, emotional resilience, and life satisfaction.

I blend cutting-edge research from neuroscience and positive psychology with personal stories to show how cultivating gratitude changes your brain’s biochemistry, improves emotional regulation, and strengthens your mental health.

Key Takeaways:
 • Gratitude is a mindset and daily practice, not just an emotion.
 • Practicing gratitude consistently reshapes the brain’s neural pathways (Zahn et al., 2009).
 • Gratitude activates brain areas associated with moral cognition and emotional regulation.
 • Small, daily acts of gratitude dramatically boost happiness and life satisfaction (Emmons & McCullough, 2003).
 • Gratitude fosters deeper connections, stronger self-esteem, and long-term well-being.

Chapters:
00:00 – The Essence of Gratitude
02:57 – The Science Behind Gratitude
04:42 – The Neuroscience of Gratitude
07:39 – The Impact of Gratitude on Well-Being
10:32 – Transforming Perspective Through Gratitude
13:53 – Practical Steps to Cultivate Gratitude

Cited Research:
 • Zahn, R., Garrido, G., Moll, J., & Grafman, J. (2009). Individual differences in posterior cortical volume correlate with proneness to pride and gratitude. NeuroImage. Link
 • Emmons, R.A., & McCullough, M.E. (2003). Counting blessings versus burdens: An experimental investigation of gratitude and subjective well-being in daily life. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology. Link

item.title: This Is Why You’re Burnt Out: Fitness, Overthinking & Mental Health with Noah Tanner (Big Fella) | 60
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 60
Guesting Noah Tanner  @biggfellabrand  

In this episode of the Grateful Podcast, Noah Tanner, aka The Big Fella, and I discussed the importance of simplicity in fitness, the challenges of overthinking, and the need for mental health awareness in the fitness journey. We explored the duality of gratitude and ambition, emphasizing that true fulfillment comes from balancing the two. Noah shared insights on celebrating small wins, the significance of authenticity in communication, and the importance of creating something meaningful in life. Our conversation highlighted the disconnect between creators and the workforce, urging listeners to recognize their achievements and prioritize self-care. 

Takeaways:
Keep it simple to avoid burnout.
Overthinking complicates fitness journeys.
Celebrate small wins to build confidence.
Productivity should focus on fulfillment, not just tasks.
Mental health is crucial in fitness success.
Authenticity resonates with audiences.
Create something to find fulfillment.
Figure out what you would regret if you were on your deathbed, and do that.
Gratitude and ambition can coexist.
Recognize the importance of self-care.
The fitness industry needs a mindset shift.

item.title: Why Faith Is Making a Comeback (Especially for Gen Z) – with Ben Hancock | 59
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner 
Episode 59
Guesting Ben Hancock

In this episode of the Grateful Podcast, I had the pleasure of engaging in a deep conversation with Ben Hancock, host of the podcast 'For All The Saints.' We explored various themes surrounding faith, spirituality, and the role of community in religious practices. The discussion delved into the differences and similarities between various belief systems, the resurgence of interest in spirituality among younger generations, and the importance of personal faith in overcoming life's challenges. We also touched on the relationship between science and faith, the impact of technology on spirituality, and the significance of community in fostering a sense of belonging and support. 

If you want to know what the future holds for faith, this is the episode for you.

Here were my main takeaways:
The podcast emphasizes the importance of sharing and reviewing to spread the message of gratitude.
A welcoming environment for diverse beliefs is crucial for understanding.
People often focus on differences in beliefs rather than similarities.
The Latter Day Saints have unique beliefs about the nature of God.
There is a resurgence of interest in religious practices among younger generations.
Spirituality and organized religion can complement each other.
Community plays a vital role in faith and support.
Hypocrisy exists in all faiths, and it's important to differentiate between faith and its members.
Faith can help individuals overcome challenges and build resilience.
Optimizing for fulfillment rather than external success leads to greater happiness.

item.title: Answering The World's Hardest Questions At 18 | 58
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 58

At 18, I don’t have all the answers — but I’m asking the questions most people are afraid of.

Who am I really?
What’s “good” or “bad”?
Why does love matter?
What’s the meaning of life?
And how the hell do we live it right?

This episode is a dive into the big stuff — the deep, un-Googleable questions. The kind of things that keep you up at night but also move you closer to who you’re meant to become.

It’s raw, personal, and grounded in curiosity. I’m not trying to be your teacher — I’m just someone walking alongside you, sharing what I’m learning.

⸻

🧠 What You’ll Take Away:
 • Identity isn’t something you are — it’s something you chase
 • Good people often endure pain that shapes their character
 • Love is real, and it connects us in ways logic can’t explain
 • The meaning of life might be simpler than we think: help others rise
 • Curiosity is the fuel for real, personal growth
 • You don’t need all the answers — just the courage to ask the right questions

⸻

🎯 Sound Bites:

“Good people seek out the bad things.”
“Difficulty defines who we become.”
“You should always be learning.”
“Most people live their lives 15 minutes at a time.”
“The right life? It’s the one that aligns with your values.”

⸻

🗺️ Chapters:

00:00 — Exploring Identity and Change
04:20 — The Nature of Goodness and Hardship
07:39 — Understanding Love
10:04 — The Meaning of Life
11:33 — Living a Right Life
14:46 — The Journey of Curiosity

⸻

🎧 Available on Spotify, Apple Podcasts, and YouTube.
This one’s for the deep thinkers — and the ones still figuring it out.

item.title: The Science of Effective Leadership with Dr. Kevin Gazzara | 57
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 57
Guesting Dr. Kevin Gazzara

Free assessment giveaway: magnaleader.co/GIFT

In this episode of the Grateful Podcast, I had the pleasure of speaking with Dr. Kevin Gazzara, a leadership expert and educator, about the essential qualities of effective leadership. We discussed the importance of communication, self-worth, and persistence in building trust and developing teams. Dr. Gazzara shares insights from his extensive experience at Intel and emphasizes the significance of understanding one's strengths and leveraging them in a leadership role. The conversation also explores the concept of the task quotient and how to create a fulfilling work environment that fosters growth and development.

My key takeaways:
The best leaders are the best communicators.
Developing others is a key trait of great leaders.
Self-worth and persistence are crucial for success.
Experience builds trust with clients and teams.
Effective communication fosters team development.
Understanding your strengths enhances leadership effectiveness.
Creating a culture of growth is essential for teams.
Task switching can be purposeful and productive.
Identifying your ideal task mixture leads to fulfillment.
Nurturing your talents is vital for personal growth.

item.title: Mastering Time: Carl Pullein on Productivity and Purpose | 56
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 56
Guesting Carl Pullein

Productivity isn't just getting more done in less time, it is about "majoring in major things" and creating something tangible.

In this episode of the Grateful Podcast, I speak with time management expert Carl Pullein about the intricacies of productivity, creativity, and personal development. We discuss the importance of protecting creative time, balancing organization with action, and the significance of identifying core work and priorities. Carl shares his journey of building an online brand, emphasizing the need for patience and the duality of gratitude and ambition in pursuing one's passions. The conversation highlights the essential elements of sleep, movement, and diet for effective productivity, and the importance of finding what truly matters in life.

Here are my key takeaways: 
Protect your creative time to maximize productivity.
Balancing organization and action is crucial for success.
Overcoming overwhelm requires establishing routines and practices.
Identify your core work to prioritize effectively.
Patience is key in building an online brand.
Success often comes from consistent, small efforts over time.
Finding your purpose can lead to greater fulfillment.
Gratitude can enhance your perspective on life and work.
Recognizing what's important helps in managing distractions.
Creating something tangible can boost your mental well-being.

Identify your core work to prioritize effectively.
Patience is key in building an online brand.
Success often comes from consistent, small efforts over time.
Finding your purpose can lead to greater fulfillment.
Gratitude can enhance your perspective on life and work.
Recognizing what's important helps in managing distractions.
Creating something tangible can boost your mental well-being.

Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 55

In this episode, I discussed the importance of personal responsibility and the power individuals have in shaping their lives. He emphasizes the need to love the journey of self-improvement, overcome internal barriers, and prioritize true rest over distractions. I also highlight the significance of trusting oneself and taking action toward goals while embracing discomfort as a catalyst for growth.

Takeaways:
We often forget the power we have in our lives.
The person in the mirror is both our hero and villain.
We trade long-term growth for short-term comfort.
Taking ownership is crucial for personal growth.
You are your biggest barrier to success.
True rest is essential for mental clarity.
Success is about consistency in doing the right things.
Comfort can be an addiction that hinders progress.
The voice inside you can be your greatest enemy.
You have the power to create the life you desire.

item.title: Why External Success Will Never Satisfy You with John R Miles | 54
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 54
Guesting John R. Miles

I had the pleasure of speaking with John R. Miles, host of the top 0.01% podcast Passion Struck and author of the #1 bestselling book of the same name. John's story is fascinating and I was so interested in interviewing him because many of his ideas are counter to what we are conditioned to believe.
John, also a former U.S. Navy officer, was an executive at Intel, one of the largest companies in the United States at the time; he was as materially successful as he could be, and yet he still wasn't satisfied.

In this episode, I got curious with John about what led him to become "passion struck" and pivot to retaking control of his life, optimizing for fulfillment over external success and validation. We talked about the negative consequences of ambition and how they can be balanced with gratitude, and why we need to focus on changing one thing at a time for maximum effectiveness. 

This was one of the best conversations I've ever had. I can't wait to hear your feedback on it.

Here were some of my big takeaways:
Everyone deserves to be seen, valued, and significant.
You have to pick the mission that you want to take on.
Life is finite and it's a hell of a lot longer than you think.
You have to be really intentional about doing the work.
The most incredible person you'll ever meet is you.
You have to cultivate the friendships you want.
Gratitude is a very reinforcing practice.
You have time to pivot.
You have to figure out what it is you're supposed to do.
You can't do everything you want.

item.title: Break Free From Limiting Beliefs with Jason Smith | 53
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 53
Guesting Jason Smith

In this enlightening conversation, I had the pleasure of interviewing Jason Smith, a fellow podcaster and coach, about the journey of self-discovery and personal growth. We explored the challenges of navigating social media, the importance of self-awareness, and the power of journaling. Jason shares insights on overcoming limiting beliefs, the significance of asking for help, and the balance between gratitude and ambition. We discussed the fear of success, the role of community in personal development, and the continuous journey of improvement. The conversation culminates in the concept of 'the power of the pivot' and the ripple effect of personal growth on others.

Takeaways:
Self-awareness is crucial for personal growth.
Navigating social media can be draining; balance is key.
Journaling helps clarify thoughts and emotions.
Limiting beliefs can hinder potential; awareness is the first step.
Asking for help is essential for growth.
Gratitude and ambition can coexist in a fulfilling life.
Fear of success can prevent individuals from embracing change.
Community support is vital in personal development.
Continuous improvement is a lifelong journey.
The power of the pivot allows for new opportunities and growth.

item.title: The Trap of Miserable Righteousness | 52
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast
Episode 52

Are you trapped in miserable righteousness and chasing empty success?

The more I learn about humans, the more I realize just how egotistical we’re wired to be. I don’t mean that as an insult — ego clearly has some evolutionary perks — but if you want to succeed in life (especially in situations you didn’t perfectly plan for), you’ve got to break free from that automatic, self-justifying loop.

In this episode of the Grateful Podcast, I explore the concept of 'miserable righteousness'—the tendency to cling to preconceived notions and judgments that lead to unnecessary suffering. I share personal anecdotes and insights on how ego can trap us in misery and prevent us from fully engaging in experiences. I emphasize the importance of maintaining an open mind, extracting value from every situation, and cultivating a gratitude mindset to enhance personal growth and fulfillment.

Takeaways:
Many people fail before they even start due to preconceived notions.
Ego can trap us in a cycle of misery and self-justification.
Being right often comes at the cost of our happiness.
We can choose to learn from every experience, even the unpleasant ones.
Saying no to things that don't align with us allows us to say yes to what truly matters.
Our mindset can significantly affect our experiences and outcomes.
Extracting value from experiences can lead to personal growth.
Gratitude can transform our perspective on challenging situations.
We have the power to change our narrative and feel better about our circumstances.
Living with a growth mindset leads to a more fulfilling life.

Chapters

00:00 The Trap of Miserable Righteousness
06:05 Breaking Free from Ego and Misery
11:54 Extracting Value from Every Experience
18:06 Gratitude and Growth Mindset

item.dc:creator: Jack Wagoner
item.itunes:summary:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast
Episode 52

Are you trapped in miserable righteousness and chasing empty success?

The more I learn about humans, the more I realize just how egotistical we’re wired to be. I don’t mean that as an insult — ego clearly has some evolutionary perks — but if you want to succeed in life (especially in situations you didn’t perfectly plan for), you’ve got to break free from that automatic, self-justifying loop.

In this episode of the Grateful Podcast, I explore the concept of 'miserable righteousness'—the tendency to cling to preconceived notions and judgments that lead to unnecessary suffering. I share personal anecdotes and insights on how ego can trap us in misery and prevent us from fully engaging in experiences. I emphasize the importance of maintaining an open mind, extracting value from every situation, and cultivating a gratitude mindset to enhance personal growth and fulfillment.

Takeaways:
Many people fail before they even start due to preconceived notions.
Ego can trap us in a cycle of misery and self-justification.
Being right often comes at the cost of our happiness.
We can choose to learn from every experience, even the unpleasant ones.
Saying no to things that don't align with us allows us to say yes to what truly matters.
Our mindset can significantly affect our experiences and outcomes.
Extracting value from experiences can lead to personal growth.
Gratitude can transform our perspective on challenging situations.
We have the power to change our narrative and feel better about our circumstances.
Living with a growth mindset leads to a more fulfilling life.

Chapters

00:00 The Trap of Miserable Righteousness
06:05 Breaking Free from Ego and Misery
11:54 Extracting Value from Every Experience
18:06 Gratitude and Growth Mindset

item.title: The Importance of Processing Your Emotions with Sherianna Boyle | 51
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 51
Guesting Sherianna Boyle

In this episode of The Grateful Podcast, host Jack Wagoner speaks with Sherrianna Boyle, an expert in emotional detox coaching. They explore the concept of emotional detox, its importance in processing emotions, and how it can lead to personal growth and a higher state of consciousness. Sherrianna shares her unique Cleanse method for emotional processing and discusses the societal fears surrounding emotions. The conversation also touches on the connection between emotional processing and manifestation, emphasizing the collective aspect of personal growth.

Takeaways:
All emotions are good as long as they're processed.
Emotional detox is about getting rid of reactions, not emotions.
Processing emotions can lead to a sense of safety and calmness.
Anxiety is an emotion looking to be processed.
Feeling is essential for personal growth and evolution.
Manifestation should focus on the collective, not just the individual.
The Cleanse method provides a structured approach to emotional processing.
Emotions are contagious and impact our collective experience.
Daily emotional processing can lead to a more peaceful life.
We are all connected and share energy, which affects our emotional states.

item.title: The Art of Optimizing for What Matters with Jonathan Cohen | 50
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast
Episode 50
Guesting Jonathan Cohen

In this episode of the Grateful Podcast, host Jack Wagoner interviews Jonathan Cohen, an attorney, athlete, and podcaster. They discuss the balance between ambition and gratitude, the importance of mental toughness, and the journey of self-optimization. Jonathan shares insights on how to find focus, the role of discipline, and the significance of recognizing diminishing returns in personal growth. The conversation emphasizes the value of reading and learning as tools for self-improvement and the importance of understanding what one is truly optimizing for in life.

Takeaways:
Balance is a lie; focus on what matters.
Mental toughness is a practice of self-love and perseverance.
You can't have everything you want, but you can have anything you want.
Recognizing diminishing returns is crucial for personal growth.
Discipline is essential for achieving your goals.
Gratitude and ambition can coexist harmoniously.
Reading provides a deeper experience than social media.
You must name your sacrifices to understand your ambitions.
Self-optimization is a journey, not a destination.
Your mindset is earned through consistent effort and action.

item.title: Navigating Life's Paradox: Presence vs. Progress | 49
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast 
Episode 49

In this episode of the Grateful Podcast, Jack Wagoner explores the delicate balance between being present in the moment and striving for future goals. He discusses the paradox of wanting to achieve ambitious dreams while also appreciating the current life we have. Jack shares personal experiences and insights on how to cultivate gratitude and ambition simultaneously, emphasizing the importance of mindfulness and conscious decision-making in creating a fulfilling life.

Takeaways:
Balancing presence and ambition is a life's paradox.
Gratitude for the present is essential for future success.
True presence comes from letting go of attachment to goals.
The belief in a better future can cause us to miss the present.
Ease in life can be prioritized without sacrificing ambition.
Fulfillment is not solely tied to material success.
The journey to inner peace does not require extreme sacrifices.
Creating a life of true value means defining success on your own terms.
Mindfulness practices can help balance ambition and gratitude.
Every moment, good or bad, contributes to our current experience.

Navigating Life's Paradox: Presence vs. Progress
The Balance of Gratitude and Ambition

Chapters

09:44 Balancing Ambition with Conscious Gratitude
16:00 Navigating Life's Choices and Values

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 48
Guesting Brianne Rush

In this episode of the Grateful Podcast, host Jack Wagoner speaks with Brianne Rush, founder of the Independence Lab, about the importance of independence, emotional intelligence, and financial literacy. They discuss how emotional intelligence can be more valuable than expertise in career advancement, the significance of financial literacy for young people, and the impact of social media on ambition and mental health. Brianne shares her personal journey, insights on defining independence, and the importance of gratitude through life's challenges.

Takeaways:
Emotional intelligence is crucial for career success.
Financial literacy is essential for independence.
Social media can negatively impact mental health and ambition.
Independence means different things to different people.
Gratitude can stem from overcoming hardships.
Self-awareness is the first step to emotional intelligence.
Young people should learn at their own pace about finances.
It's important to have a career path that aligns with personal values.
The transition from college to career lacks guidance.
Every generation faces unique challenges that shape their experiences.

In this episode of the Grateful Podcast, host Jack Wagoner speaks with Brianne Rush, founder of the Independence Lab, about the importance of independence, emotional intelligence, and financial literacy. They discuss how emotional intelligence can be more valuable than expertise in career advancement, the significance of financial literacy for young people, and the impact of social media on ambition and mental health. Brianne shares her personal journey, insights on defining independence, and the importance of gratitude through life's challenges.

Takeaways:
Emotional intelligence is crucial for career success.
Financial literacy is essential for independence.
Social media can negatively impact mental health and ambition.
Independence means different things to different people.
Gratitude can stem from overcoming hardships.
Self-awareness is the first step to emotional intelligence.
Young people should learn at their own pace about finances.
It's important to have a career path that aligns with personal values.
The transition from college to career lacks guidance.
Every generation faces unique challenges that shape their experiences.

item.title: How To Become Truly Fulfilled with Raghunath Cappo | 47
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 47
Guesting Raghunath Ray Cappo

In this conversation, I interview Raghunath Ray Cappo, exploring his transformative journey from punk rock musician to monk and spiritual teacher. We discuss the challenges of material success, the importance of self-discovery, and the practice of Bhakti yoga. Raghunath shares insights on maintaining spiritual practices in daily life, the nature of oneness, and the illusions of material existence, emphasizing the significance of community and mindful living.

Here are my key takeaways

Self-discovery is a lifelong journey that often requires deep introspection.
Material success can lead to unexpected realizations about greed and desire.
Spiritual practices can help ground us in our true purpose and identity.
Community plays a crucial role in maintaining spiritual focus and motivation.
Bhakti yoga emphasizes love and devotion as pathways to spiritual enlightenment.
Understanding the nature of oneness can be complex but is essential for spiritual growth.
The material world can be deceptive, often leading us away from our true selves.
Spiritual enlightenment involves remembering our true nature beyond material identities.
Maintaining a spiritual practice requires intentionality and discipline in daily life.
The journey of life is temporary, and we must seek deeper meaning beyond material pursuits.

item.title: Make Positivity Go Viral: Abolish Negative Internet Culture | 46
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 46

In this episode of the Grateful Podcast, Jack Wagoner explores the human tendency to gravitate towards negativity, especially in the context of social media. He reflects on the recent success of his podcast episode with Rabbi Manus Friedman, which garnered significant views but also a wave of negative comments. Jack emphasizes the importance of positivity and understanding in conversations, advocating for a shift in focus from hate to gratitude and connection. He encourages listeners to engage in small acts of kindness and to spread positivity in their communities, highlighting that even minor gestures can make a significant impact. 

Takeaways:
Human beings are attracted to negativity over positivity.
The internet amplifies extreme views and negativity.
Positivity is essential for building a better society.
Listening to differing opinions can expand our perspectives.
Small acts of kindness can make a big difference.
We need to combat the negativity prevalent on social media.
Creating a personal connection with the audience is important.
Gratitude can change lives and perspectives.
The focus should be on what brings us together, not divides us.
We can influence others to spread positivity instead of negativity.

Chapters

00:00 The Attraction to Negativity
06:40 The Role of Positivity in Society
12:06 Transforming Negativity into Positivity
