item.title: Beyond the Plate: Food, Nature, and Meaning with Chef Evan Hennessey | 45
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 45
Guesting Evan Hennessey

In this engaging conversation, Evan Hennessey and I explore the journey of culinary passion, the importance of curiosity, and the connections we build in life. We discuss the role of nature in personal well-being, the disconnection prevalent in modern society, and the significance of authentic relationships in the restaurant industry. The dialogue also delves into the thrill of high-stress environments, learning from failure, and the fast-paced world of cooking shows, all while highlighting the impact of climbing on personal growth. In this conversation, Evan shares his journey into climbing, the importance of work-life balance, and the influence of generational perspectives on career choices. He discusses personal growth through self-discovery and the challenges within the restaurant industry's culture. Evan emphasizes the significance of community and connection through food and introduces his initiative 'Finding Thyme' aimed at reconnecting people with nature. The discussion culminates in exploring the duality of gratitude and ambition in life, highlighting how these elements can coexist to foster a fulfilling existence.

Here are my key takeaways:
Evan enjoys the journey of cooking, not just the destination.
Curiosity drives personal growth and success.
Nature helps us feel connected and grounded.
Modern society often feels disconnected from reality.
Restaurants should focus on community and connection.
Building authentic relationships is key in the restaurant industry.
Spontaneity can lead to personal growth and fulfillment.
High-stress environments can lead to flow states and focus.
Failure is a part of learning and growth.
Climbing has significantly influenced Evan's life. 
Finding a passion early in life can lead to greater fulfillment.
Work-life balance is essential for a happy life.
It's important to take your head out of the sand and engage with the world.
Your life should come before your career.
Many young people struggle to prioritize their goals due to external influences.
Personal growth often requires introspection and self-discovery.
The restaurant industry has a culture that can be detrimental to work-life balance.
Creating community through food leads to meaningful connections.
Gratitude and ambition can coexist 

Chapters
00:00 The Journey of Culinary Passion
02:53 The Importance of Curiosity and Connection
05:47 Nature's Role in Personal Well-being
09:03 The Disconnection in Modern Society
11:59 Building Authentic Connections in Restaurants
14:54 Embracing Spontaneity and Personal Growth
17:52 The Thrill of High-Stress Environments
20:46 Learning from Failure and Competition
24:07 The Fast-Paced World of Cooking Shows
27:00 The Impact of Climbing on Life
29:48 The Journey into Climbing
32:41 Finding Work-Life Balance
35:06 The Influence of Generational Perspectives
39:30 Personal Growth and Self-Discovery
42:27 The Restaurant Industry's Culture
45:18 Creating Community Through Food
53:11 Finding Thyme: Connecting with Nature
57:30 Conclusion

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 44
Guesting Mike Pridgen

In this episode of the Grateful Podcast, I speak with Mike Pridgen, an expert in sustainable health and fitness. We discuss the pervasive myths in the fitness industry, the importance of kindness in self-improvement, and the long-term journey of weight loss. Mike shares his personal experiences with weight loss and emphasizes the need for enjoyable habits rather than extreme measures. The conversation also touches on the dangers of toxic fitness culture, the impact of social media on body image, and the importance of authenticity in coaching. Ultimately, the episode encourages listeners to approach health and fitness with self-respect and kindness, while also sharing valuable insights on nutrition and the cultural influences on obesity.

My key takeaways:

Sustainable health is about self-respect, not self-punishment.
Enjoyable habits are crucial for long-term success.
The fitness industry is filled with misinformation and quick fixes.
Kindness to oneself is essential in the journey of self-improvement.
Weight loss is a long-term journey that requires patience.
Extreme fitness mentalities can lead to burnout and failure.
Processed foods are a significant issue in modern diets.
Cultural influences play a major role in obesity rates.
Authenticity in coaching is vital for building trust.
Sharing knowledge is key to helping others on their health journey.

item.title: Success Without Presence Is Empty: How Can We Savor It? | 43
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 43

How can we savor our success?

In this episode of the Grateful Podcast, I explore the relationship between success and the ability to enjoy it. I discuss the duality of gratitude and ambition, emphasizing that one can strive for better circumstances while appreciating the present. I share personal anecdotes about the struggle to be present during significant moments and highlight meditation as a crucial tool for enhancing mindfulness and presence. I reflect on the societal need for prioritizing meditation to foster a more peaceful and aware community. 

Here are the key takeaways:

Success is meaningless if we can't enjoy it.
Gratitude and ambition can coexist.
Being present is a challenge in our fast-paced lives.
Meditation can help us become more present.
Prioritizing meditation is essential for cherishing success.
Empty successes lack inherent value without presence.
Meditation is a skill that improves with practice.
The benefits of meditation can transform our daily lives.
Curiosity about deeper meditation can lead to greater peace.
Societal change is possible through collective meditation practices.

04:37 The Challenge of Being Present
07:49 Meditation as a Tool for Presence

item.title: Finding Independence Through Entrepreneurship with Judah Payeur | 42
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 42
Guesting Judah Payeur

In this conversation, Judah Payeur shares his entrepreneurial journey, starting from his early experiences with shoe reselling to his current ventures in Amazon and caffeine pouches. The discussion emphasizes the importance of pursuing dreams, the evolution of business ideas, and the challenges faced by young entrepreneurs. Judah reflects on the misconceptions surrounding online business opportunities and the drive for independence that fuels his passion for entrepreneurship. The conversation also touches on the lessons learned from school and work experiences, highlighting the balance between education and entrepreneurial pursuits. In this conversation, Judah and I discuss our experiences navigating high school and college while balancing business ventures. They share insights on time management, the importance of networking, and the challenges of content creation through podcasting. The discussion also touches on future aspirations and the entrepreneurial mindset, emphasizing the need to pursue dreams despite uncertainties.

Takeaways

If you have a dream, go after it to avoid regret.
Entrepreneurship can start at a young age, even in school.
The journey of entrepreneurship often begins with a simple idea.
Prioritizing time is crucial for balancing school and business.
Many people limit themselves by not pursuing their passions.
Online business opportunities can be misleading.
The drive for independence is a strong motivator for entrepreneurs.
Working with others can be challenging but rewarding.
Real success comes from doing what you love on your own terms.
Belief in your vision is essential for entrepreneurial success. High school can be challenging, especially when balancing personal interests and academic responsibilities.
College requires a different level of commitment and effort compared to high school.
Time management is crucial for balancing business, school, and personal life.
Networking is essential for business growth and personal development.
Podcasting can be a valuable tool for building relationships and sharing knowledge.
Creating content requires dedication and can be a learning experience.
The entrepreneurial mindset involves taking risks and pursuing multiple interests.
It's important to focus on a specific niche to effectively reach your target audience.
Future aspirations can be uncertain, but having a clear vision helps guide decisions.
Pursuing dreams is more fulfilling than living with regret.

Chapters

03:13 The Entrepreneurial Journey Begins
05:49 Evolving Business Ventures
09:13 Navigating the Amazon Marketplace
11:55 The Reality of Online Business Gurus
15:04 The Drive Behind Entrepreneurship

39:18 Balancing College and Business
43:10 Daily Routines and Time Management

Jonathan Goodman

In this episode of the Grateful Podcast, I speak with Jonathan Goodman, an entrepreneur and author, about the evolving landscape of business in the digital age. They discuss the importance of trust and reputation, the challenges of standing out in a noisy market, and the pursuit of greatness through focused effort. Goodman shares insights from his journey as an author and the significance of building genuine relationships in business. The conversation emphasizes the need for introspection and the value of engaging with audiences on a personal level.

Here were my key takeaways:

Trust and reputation are invaluable assets in business.
Preparation is key to making the most of opportunities.
In a noisy digital landscape, focus on what truly matters.
Success is a result of becoming great at one thing.
Building relationships is essential for long-term success.
The journey to authorship requires dedication and focus.
Writing is a process that requires discipline and consistency.
Engaging with your audience can lead to meaningful connections.
Finding opportunities often means looking beyond the obvious.
Introspection is crucial for personal and professional growth.

item.title: The REAL Reason You Struggle To Maintain Your Motivation | 40
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast 
Episode 40

In this episode of The Grateful Podcast, I explore the journey of motivation and the inevitable plateaus that come with personal growth. He emphasizes the importance of gratitude and balance in the pursuit of success, arguing that what got you to a certain point may not be enough to take you further. Jack reflects on the cultural obsession with success and the need for self-fulfillment, encouraging listeners to appreciate their current lives while striving for more. Ultimately, he advocates for a mindset that values the journey over the outcome, promoting a healthier approach to ambition and personal development.

Here are my takeaways:
Motivation can wane after initial success.
Plateaus are a natural part of growth.
You need to adapt your approach to continue improving.
Gratitude is essential for a balanced mindset.
Success does not always equate to fulfillment.
Cultural pressures can distort our view of success.
Finding joy in the journey is crucial.
Ambition should coexist with appreciation for the present.
Pushing too hard can lead to burnout.
Self-worth should not be tied to external validation.

item.title: What Does The Future Hold For Gen-Z with Elliot Bewick | 39
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 39
Guesting Elliot Bewick, host of The Next Generation Podcast

In this episode of the Grateful Podcast, I engage in a thought-provoking conversation with Elliott Bewick, exploring the unique challenges faced by Gen Z in a rapidly evolving digital landscape. They discuss the paradox of living in a time of unprecedented success while grappling with feelings of dissatisfaction and disconnection. The conversation delves into the impact of social media on relationships, the struggle for authenticity in content creation, and the moral complexities of navigating a world filled with instant gratification. Ultimately, they emphasize the importance of gratitude, high standards, and the pursuit of meaningful connections in a society that often prioritizes superficial engagement. Here were my biggest takeaways from the conversation:

Takeaways

We are victims of our own success right now.
Things are subjectively bad, but objectively they've never been this good.
We're suffering from contending with overabundance.
The events that keep on being fed to us don't give us the ability to see these slow burners.
You need not just the carrot, but the stick.
You can still be your authentic self by putting out amazing polished content.
It's difficult to have that historical context.
You have to stay curious, stay open and never die on the hill of something.
You need to be the type of person that puts the truth over discomfort.
You can build upon something you love.

item.title: Applying Ancient Wisdom to Modern Problems with Rabbi Manis Friedman | 38
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 38

Rabbi Manis Friedman


In this enlightening conversation, Rabbi Manis Friedman shares his insights on the intersection of ancient wisdom and modern challenges, particularly focusing on the decline of religious belief among younger generations. He discusses the importance of trust in authority, the complexity of morality, and the dual nature of religion as both a source of guidance and potential toxicity. The dialogue emphasizes the need for purpose in life and the role of compassion while also addressing the misconceptions surrounding atheism and the nature of human goodness. Rabbi Friedman encourages a return to fundamental truths that have stood the test of time, advocating for a life of service and understanding. 

I must address the fact that I do not wholeheartedly agree with everything Rabbi Friedman said, and I am not a member of the Jewish faith. However, I believe that it is important for everyone to try to understand where others are coming from, and this conversation helped me do that. I am, personally, an atheist-leaning agnostic open to spiritual interpretation. 

Here is what I took away from today's conversation:

Ancient wisdom is tested and not an experiment.
The decline of religious belief is linked to a rejection of the old.
Anxiety stems from uncertainty about life and purpose.
Atheism often arises from fear of being wrong.
Morality cannot be invented; it must be recognized.
Religion can be toxic when it replaces true authority.
Humility is essential in leadership and spirituality.
Compassion must align with justice and truth.
Life is not about fulfilling personal needs but serving a greater purpose.
The future of humanity lies in recognizing our need to serve rather than being needy.

Chapters

00:00 Exploring Ancient Wisdom for Modern Problems
04:58 The Decline of Religious Affiliation
12:40 Questioning Authority and Seeking Truth
20:48 The Dual Nature of Religion: Positivity and Violence
29:05 Understanding Modern Anti-Semitism

37:17 Understanding Belief and Atheism
42:52 Purpose and Service in Life
47:02 Compassion and Its Complexities
49:58 The Nature of Good and Evil
55:12 Justice and Compassion in Religion
58:39 The Future of Humanity and Purpose
01:01:42 Outro

item.title: The Difference Between Intellectual Understanding and Understanding + Rest Prioritization | 37
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner

Episode 37

In this episode, I discuss the critical importance of rest and how it impacts productivity and health. He reflects on his recent illness, emphasizing the need to prioritize rest and the cultural misconceptions surrounding productivity. Jack also explores the difference between understanding concepts intellectually and embodying them through action, highlighting that true growth comes from applying knowledge rather than just knowing it. He concludes with a reminder to stay grateful, regardless of external circumstances.

Takeaways:
You need to prioritize rest for recovery.
Rest is an investment in future productivity.
Procrastinating rest can lead to worse outcomes.
Cultural perceptions often glorify overworking.
Finding balance is essential for personal growth.
Trial and error helps in understanding optimal actions.
Intellectual understanding is different from practical application.
Knowledge alone does not lead to change; action is necessary.
Gratitude can transform your perspective on challenges.
Your identity is separate from your circumstances.

item.title: Navigating Life With a GRATITUDE ATTITUDE - David George Brooke | 36
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 36

In this episode of the Grateful Podcast, I speak with David George-Brooke, known as 'that gratitude guy.' They explore the transformative power of gratitude, discussing how it can shift mindsets, enhance resilience, and improve overall well-being. David shares personal anecdotes and insights from his decades of experience in studying and teaching gratitude. The conversation delves into the importance of conscious gratitude practices, the impact of social media on self-perception, and the necessity of taking chances in life. David emphasizes that gratitude is not just a feeling but a choice that can lead to a more fulfilling life. In this conversation, David George Brooke shares his insights on finding purpose in life, the importance of gratitude, and the impact of lifelong learning. He discusses practical steps to discover one's purpose, the significance of embracing technology, and the value of maintaining a disciplined morning routine. David emphasizes the need to balance gratitude with ambition and reflects on the lessons learned from adversity. He also shares personal anecdotes about his journey and the importance of leaving a legacy.

Here were my biggest takeaways from the conversation:
Gratitude can transform your perspective on life.
Happiness is an internal state, not dependent on external factors.
Writing down what you're grateful for reinforces positive thinking.
A gratitude attitude helps combat negativity and promotes mental health.
Conscious gratitude practice is essential during tough times.
Social media can amplify feelings of inadequacy and comparison.
Taking chances in life leads to personal growth and fulfillment.
The most important relationship is with yourself.
Starting with small steps can lead to discovering your purpose.
Shifting your purpose can bring new life and energy.
Creating lists of desires can help prioritize goals.
It's never too late to pursue your dreams, as shown by many successful figures.
Adversity often teaches the most valuable lessons.
Maintaining a disciplined routine can enhance productivity.
Gratitude can coexist with ambition and drive.
Leaving a positive legacy is a key aspect of life.

item.title: The Hustle: Balancing Passion & Growth at 16 with Gavin Beauregard | 35
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

Gavin Beauregard on The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 35

In this episode of the Grateful Podcast, Gavin Beauregard and I discuss the importance of authenticity in content creation, the journey of entrepreneurship, and the role of social media in personal growth. They explore the challenges of finding a supportive community, navigating social media addiction, and the significance of building connections in new environments. The conversation emphasizes the need for individuals to be true to themselves and to pursue their passions while also recognizing the impact of their surroundings on their personal development. In this conversation, we speak on the journey of content creation, emphasizing the importance of building connections, developing skills, and the balance between monetization and personal growth. Gavin shares insights on the significance of consistency in producing content, and I explore various business models for podcasts and the commitment required for long-term success. The dialogue also touches on the joy of creative endeavors and innovative ideas for branding and content creation. I really enjoyed talking to Gavin. I learned a lot. Here are my key takeaways from our conversation:

Takeaways

Building your own style is crucial for uniqueness.
Authenticity in content creation attracts the right audience.
Ambition should be balanced with gratitude for the present.
Social media can be both a tool for growth and a source of addiction.
Finding a supportive community is essential for personal growth.
Isolation can be a part of the journey to success.
Surrounding yourself with the right people influences your path.
Navigating social media requires awareness and boundaries.
Pursuing passions should come before monetary gain.
The journey of entrepreneurship is often non-linear and exploratory. Building connections through content creation is essential.
It's important to focus on skill development over immediate monetization.
Consistency and repetition are key to improving content quality.
Exploring different business models can help sustain a podcast.
Long-term commitment is crucial for podcast growth.
Finding joy in creative endeavors leads to more fulfilling work.
Gratitude and a positive mindset are vital for success.

item.title: Feeding Obsession Through Scarcity: The Secret to Greatness | 34
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 34

Everything that you love, really love, is in scarcity. Make it the same with your passion.

In this episode of the Grateful Podcast, I discuss the balance between pursuing ambitions and living in the moment. He shares personal experiences from a recent rock climbing competition and emphasizes the importance of maintaining passion for one's work while also enjoying life. Jack explores the concept of scarcity in passion, the challenges of self-doubt, and the gamble of pursuing dreams without guaranteed success. He encourages listeners to feed multiple passions and build a supportive community around their endeavors.

Takeaways

Building on appreciation is more effective than striving away from negativity.
It's important to find a balance between work and fun.
Maintaining scarcity in passion helps keep the excitement alive.
Self-doubt is a common experience, even for confident individuals.
Hard work does not guarantee success, but it is necessary to try.
Setting timeframes for commitments can help prevent quitting too early.
You can pursue multiple passions without sacrificing relationships.
Community support is vital for personal growth and motivation.
Sharing experiences can help build a supportive network.
Staying grateful is essential for a fulfilling life.

Chapters

07:44 Navigating Self-Doubt and Perseverance
12:59 The Gamble of Pursuing Dreams
18:34 Upcoming Episodes and Community Building

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 33
David Lorimer from today.iam.grateful

In this episode of the Grateful Podcast, host Jack Wagoner speaks with David Lorimer, a prominent figure in the gratitude movement. They discuss the importance of gratitude in personal growth, the contrast between negativity and positivity, and how to reframe one's perspective to find gratitude in everyday life. David shares his journey of overcoming mental health struggles through gratitude practices and emphasizes the need to appreciate the little things in life. The conversation also touches on cultural conditioning towards negativity and the role of media in shaping our perspectives on gratitude and positivity. In this conversation, David discusses the transformative power of gratitude in personal growth and mental health. He emphasizes the importance of reframing perspectives on challenges and the cultural conditioning that often leads to a negative outlook on life. David advocates for the idea that happiness is a choice and can be cultivated through gratitude, even in difficult circumstances. He also explores how gratitude can serve as a societal change agent, promoting positivity and emotional well-being in communities.

item.title: How Your Parents’ Mental Health Impacts Yours with Deb Armstrong Branch | 32
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 32

Deb's Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/happychild2happyparent/ 

In this episode of the Grateful Podcast, host Jack Wagoner speaks with Deborah Armstrong-Branch, a specialist nurse from England, about the critical role of emotional development in early childhood. They discuss the importance of allowing children to express a range of emotions, the impact of attachment styles on future relationships, and the balance between kindness and setting boundaries in parenting. Deborah emphasizes the need for emotional vocabulary and the dangers of over-parenting, particularly in the context of modern pressures such as social media and screen time. The conversation highlights the significance of self-care for parents and offers practical advice for raising resilient and emotionally intelligent children.

Takeaways

Encouraging constant happiness in children can create pressure.
Emotional intelligence is crucial from a young age.
Attachment styles formed in childhood affect adult relationships.
Parents' emotional expressions influence children's emotional development.
Over-parenting can lead to children lacking resilience.
Children need to learn to cope with adversity.
Establishing routines and boundaries is essential for children.
Screens can hinder children's creativity and social skills.
Talking about feelings should be normalized in families.
Self-care for parents is vital for effective parenting.

item.title: The Beautiful Illusion of Curiosity: How To Construct Your Reality With the Glue For Success | 31
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Grateful Podcast

Episode 31

🎙️ Episode Summary:

In this solo episode, I explore the fascinating idea that the reality we accept as absolute truth may, in fact, be built on nothing more than widely agreed-upon illusions. Using Isaac Newton’s discovery of the laws of physics as a case study, I dive into how curiosity shapes human progress and dictates the foundations of our shared reality. What if Newton was wrong? Would we even know? And what does that mean for the way we experience life?


I also discuss the duality of gratitude and ambition—how we balance appreciation for the present with the drive to create a better future. Plus, I break down the difference between push vs. pull success and how understanding this can change the way you approach your goals.


🔹 Topics Covered in This Episode:

• How curiosity shapes reality and why truth might not be as “absolute” as we think

• The power of foundational beliefs in human progress

• The paradox of gratitude and ambition

• Push vs. pull success: which one leads to a more fulfilling life?


🔔 Episodes This Week:

item.title: BREAKING The CHAINS of People Pleasing with Nick Pollard (The People Displeaser) | 30
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

Nick Pollard on Breaking FREE From People Pleasing
The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 30

In this episode of the Grateful Podcast, host Jack Wagoner engages in a deep conversation with Nick Pollard, a coach and speaker known as the People Displeaser. They explore the pervasive issue of people-pleasing, its roots in the desire for acceptance, and how social media exacerbates this behavior. Nick shares his personal journey of overcoming people-pleasing tendencies and emphasizes the importance of setting boundaries and living authentically. The discussion also touches on the paradox of seeking approval from others while neglecting one's own needs, the significance of imperfection, and the role of honesty in relationships. Ultimately, the episode encourages listeners to embrace their true selves and make decisions that prioritize their own happiness.

This was a truly amazing conversation for me as my entire family battles with the people-pleasing "addiction," as Nick calls it. I have spent most of my conscious life either falling hopelessly victim to this state or trying to break free from it. Nick is incredibly knowledgable, as evidenced by his words in this conversation. I learned so much, here were my big takeaways:

People-pleasing is rooted in the desire for acceptance.
Social media amplifies feelings of inadequacy and comparison.
Overcoming people-pleasing requires consistent effort and self-discovery.
Setting boundaries is crucial for personal well-being.
A Bill of Rights can help individuals assert their needs.
People-pleasing is a lifelong journey, not a one-time fix.
Authenticity attracts genuine relationships.
Feelings are impermanent; decisions can have lasting consequences.
Honesty and kindness are intertwined in relationships.
Embracing imperfection leads to deeper connections.

item.title: Paving Your Own Path— How Bunkt Became an Artist at 43 | 29
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

Watch on YouTube:
Paving Your Own Path— How Bunkt Became an Artist at 43
The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 29

Bunkt_ has made art the focal point of his life; he found it at 43, he says, but that just proves that it is never too late to give up on yourself and pursue your dreams.

In this episode, Jack interviews his dad, Bunkt, an artist who found his passion and purpose at age 43. They dive into his creative process, how he initially emulated Basquiat before developing his own style, and the impact of daily creative work on his fulfillment. Bunkt shares insights on consistency, personal time, and the long-term rewards of pursuing what you love. They explore the question: Is your creative pursuit the key to a more fulfilled life?

Personally, this was one of my favorite conversations I have ever had. It was admittedly a little weird at first to speak with my dad in front of cameras: we talk all the time, but the changed environment was a bit off-putting. However, by the end, we were very comfortable, and I loved how the conversation turned out. I am so proud of my dad for going after what he loves in life. Seeing him pursue art as his full-time thing inspires me to settle for nothing less than my dreams. I know that anything is possible in life, and I owe that a lot to my dad. 

I have the best dad I could ever ask for; I am so grateful.

I hope you enjoy the conversation.

item.title: How Being PSYCHED Will TRANSFORM Your Life With Nathan Bigelow | 27
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

How Being PSYCHED Will Transform Your Life With Nathan Bigelow
The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner Episode 25


Nathan Bigelow is a 18-year-old high school senior from Dover, New Hampshire. He excels in every area of his life— a top student, a number one varsity tennis player, an avid rock climber and coach, and an overall smart young man. More importantly, Nathan Bigelow has been my best friend for the last 14 years. We don't touch on it in the episode, but everyone deserves this type of friendship— having a friend who is totally invested in your life just as you are in theirs makes life more fun and valuable. 


This is truly one of my favorite conversations I’ve ever had. We dive into everything from how you can live your life with more psych and excitement, to the power of abstaining from social media as a teenager. I think you’ll love it.

We started off the conversation by talking about how you can foster more psych in your life. Psych is the contagious energy that some people have when they are just infatuated by the excitement of life. Nathan is great at staying present in the moment and generating excitement for just about anything, including the things others would dread. This shows in his discipline— waking up at 5 AM before school to run and work out. 


This leads us to start talking about early risers and late to bedders. We dive into our own schedules and how some of us tend naturally toward one thing, but would rather force ourselves to do another.

We then go into social media, my favorite topic of this podcast. Nathan has never had social media. As a seventeen-year-old, this is extremely rare. We explore the benefits this has on his life and how his creativity is unlocked by the lack of comparison he has to the top “0.01%”. 

We ask the question: is social media a drug? We explore the addiction that so many of our peers have and how detrimental it is to our generation.

We then denounce nihilism. Nathan believes that each and every moment could open a door to a better life. Life is a gift— although we may never dent the universe as a whole, we can make an impact on the small circle of people around us. That is enough. 

Overall, this is an episode about loving life.

Links & Resources Mentioned (not sponsored):

  • The Compound Effect by Darren Hardy

This book is mentioned by both Jack and Nathan. It talks about the power of compounding habits over time. It’s a game-changer.

  • Ray Bradbury books (Nathan’s favorite author)
  • LMNT Electrolytes: the best electrolyte drink in the game. Jack has started his day with an LMNT packet every day for the past 2 years.

item.title: Pursuing Passion: The Key to True Wealth | The Grateful Podcast Episode 26
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

Pursuing Passion: The Key to True Wealth
The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner

Episode 26


In this episode, Jack Wagoner emphasizes the importance of pursuing passion over monetary gain. He discusses how loving what you do can lead to greater happiness and wealth accumulation, supported by research findings. Jack shares his personal experiences with business and the lessons learned about fulfillment and success. He challenges societal norms that prioritize financial stability over personal satisfaction, advocating for a life driven by passion and purpose.

If you enjoyed this episode, it would mean the world to me if you shared it with someone who you think would enjoy or benefit from the message. You could also support the show by leaving a review down below!

takeaways

  • Passion leads to wealth, but wealth doesn't guarantee happiness.
  • Loving your job correlates with higher income and satisfaction.
  • Those who love their work accumulate wealth faster than those who don't.
  • Finding a job you love can lead to quicker financial success.
  • Society often misguides individuals to prioritize money over fulfillment.
  • Personal experiences can shape our understanding of success and happiness.
  • It's essential to pursue what lights you up in life.
  • You don't need to sacrifice well-being for financial gain.
  • Life is too short to spend it on unfulfilling work.
  • Challenging societal expectations can lead to a more fulfilling life.


Chapters

00:00 The Pursuit of Passion Over Wealth
04:48 The Importance of Loving Your Work
10:04 Redefining Success and Happiness
15:08 Challenging Societal Norms on Work and Wealth

item.title: Rock Climbing Addiction and Building Around Passion with Ben Mills | 25
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

Rock Climbing Addiction and Building Around Passion with Ben Mills

The Grateful Podcast With Jack Wagoner

Episode 25

Join us for an inspiring climb to the top as aspiring pro climber Ben Mills takes us on his captivating journey from initial skepticism to full-blown climbing addiction.

Discover how he harnessed the power of mindset, visualization, and authentic content creation to scale the heights of social media success and climb towards his dreams of becoming a professional climber.

Learn Ben’s strategies for overcoming mental roadblocks, cultivating unshakeable confidence, and turning his passion into a potential career. Get motivated to conquer your own climbing—and life—challenges through his insights on balancing discipline, tapping into motivation, and reaching the summit of your goals.

Whether you’re a seasoned climber or just starting your ascent, this episode will inspire you to reach new peaks in your own journey.

Timestamps

00:10 – Ben Mills, aspiring pro climber and content creator

01:34 – Ben’s background and childhood

02:44 – The addictive nature of rock climbing

05:40 – Comp climbing vs. outdoor climbing

07:12 – Learning confidence through climbing and life

11:37 – Ben’s journey in content creation

item.title: Life Flies— Why Appreciating Your Progress Fuels Growth | The Grateful Podcast Episode 24
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

Life Flies— Why Appreciating Your Progress Fuels Growth
The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
Episode 24

In this solo episode, I explore a lesson life keeps trying to teach me: the importance of slowing down and truly appreciating our progress. For many of us chasing success, it’s easy to rush past our wins and immediately focus on the next goal. But what happens when we don’t let our victories sink in?

I share my personal struggle with celebrating success and reflect on my best semester yet as a high school senior—balancing school, running a business, and applying to colleges. Through these experiences, I’ve realized that rewarding ourselves for hard work isn’t just nice—it’s necessary. Positive reinforcement is proven to build habits, and taking time to acknowledge our wins fuels future growth.

This episode also dives into the role of challenging ourselves and how confirmation bias can stunt our growth. I discuss my own journey of studying in France and how stepping outside my comfort zone has made me a better student and person. If you’ve ever felt like you’re moving too fast to enjoy life, this episode will remind you to pause, reflect, and celebrate every step of the way.

If this episode resonates with you, share it with a friend who needs a reminder to slow down and celebrate their wins. Don’t forget to leave a review and subscribe for more episodes on living with intention and chasing your dreams.

What You’ll Learn in This Episode:

• Why it’s hard for high achievers to celebrate their progress.

• How rewarding yourself for hard work can boost productivity and build habits.

• Simple ways to slow down and reflect after a success.

• How confirmation bias stunts growth—and how to challenge yourself to keep evolving.

• Personal stories about balancing school, business, and big dreams.


Key Takeaways:

1. Life moves fast, but success is sweeter when you pause to let it marinate.

2. Positive reinforcement isn’t just nice; it’s a psychological necessity for habit-building.

3. Growth happens when we step outside our comfort zone and challenge our assumptions.

item.title: Finding Your Why: The Duality of Gratitude and Ambition— The Grateful Podcast Episode 23
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

Episode 23 of the Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner

If you enjoyed this episode it would mean the world to me if you left a review so I could understand what you like and don't like about my episodes.

Additionally, I kindly ask that you share this episode with someone that you think would appreciate it.

In this episode of The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner, we explore the profound connection between knowing your “why” and finding fulfillment in both your dreams and daily life. Jack dives into the duality of gratitude and ambition, discussing how to balance the joy of the present moment with the drive to achieve big goals.


Have you ever realized the thing you’re working toward might already be within reach? Jack unpacks this transformative idea, offering insights into how self-awareness can shift your perspective and bring clarity to your journey. He also emphasizes the importance of loving the process rather than fixating solely on the end goal.


This episode is packed with actionable advice, personal anecdotes, and thought-provoking ideas to help you live with greater purpose, balance, and joy. Whether you’re chasing a big dream or simply trying to find meaning in everyday life, this conversation will inspire you to rethink how you approach your ambitions.


Topics Covered in This Episode:

1.Why finding your “why” is essential

•How understanding your purpose can fuel motivation and clarity.

2.The duality of gratitude and ambition

•Why you need both gratitude for the present and ambition for the future to thrive.

3.Realizing your goals might already be available to you

•A shift in mindset: Are you chasing something you already have?

4.Loving the process vs. focusing on the end goal

•How falling in love with the journey can lead to lasting fulfillment.

5.Practical tips to embrace the process

•How to cultivate gratitude and stay present while still pursuing your dreams.


Key Takeaways:

•Your “why” is the foundation of meaningful ambition—without it, even success can feel hollow.

•Gratitude and ambition are not opposites; they are two sides of the same coin.

•Sometimes, the things we chase—happiness, connection, purpose—are already available to us if we shift our perspective.

•The journey matters more than the destination; loving the process is the key to sustained joy.


Links & Resources Mentioned:

•Follow Jack on Instagram for daily inspiration: https://www.instagram.com/jack_wagoner_/ 

•Learn more about Jack’s coaching and free 15-minute calls: https://calendly.com/jackcwagoner/30min

•Subscribe to The Grateful Podcast to never miss an episode.


Episode Challenge:

Take 5 minutes today to brainstorm and write down the things you are most grateful for in your life.

What brings you the most joy? What relationships do you value the most? 

Let yourself feel gratitude for these aspects of your life.

item.title: How Creativity Compounds: Humanity’s Superpower Explained | The Grateful Podcast 22
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

Albert Einstein once said creativity is “intelligence having fun,” but what if it’s more than that? What if creativity is the core trait that defines us as humans? In this episode of The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner, we explore how creativity has shaped history, drives innovation, and could hold the key to our collective future.

Creativity isn’t just about painting or making music—it’s about solving problems, innovating, and driving progress. From the fire-starting hunter-gatherers to the Sumerians’ groundbreaking agricultural canals, humanity’s greatest advancements have been rooted in creative thinking. What’s fascinating is that creativity compounds. As new ideas emerge, the foundation for even greater innovation is laid.

But here’s the question: why doesn’t the American education system prioritize creativity in the same way it does math or science? Why are art and music classes treated as secondary when they’re the very essence of what makes us human? In this episode, I dive into the roots of this imbalance and challenge the stereotypes of “creative people” vs. “math people.”

We’ll also discuss the double-edged sword of creativity: the endless flow of ideas can be a gift—but also a curse, making it hard to stay focused or committed to one vision. Drawing insights from Ray Dalio’s Principles, we uncover how resilience can help creative minds thrive, turning dreams into reality despite the struggles along the way.

Whether you’re a budding artist, an innovator, or someone simply curious about the human mind, this episode is packed with thought-provoking insights that will inspire you to embrace your creativity fully.

What You’ll Learn in This Episode:
•How creativity built civilizations and shapes innovation today.
•The reasons behind America’s flawed approach to creative education.
•Why creativity and resilience go hand-in-hand.
•Practical tips to channel your creative energy effectively.

item.title: If You’ve Got a Dream, You Go: Harrison Goodell’s Insights on Pursuing a Career in Music | 21
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

 If You’ve Got a Dream, You Go: Harrison Goodell’s Insights on Pursuing a Career in Music


🎙️ Guest: Harrison Goodell

🌟 Follow Harrison: Instagram


What does it truly take to pursue your passion and turn it into your life’s work? In this episode of The Grateful Podcast, I sit down with the talented singer-songwriter Harrison Goodell, who’s boldly chasing his dream in the music industry. Harrison shares how he made the decision to go all in on his creative career, without relying on a backup plan—a risk that many shy away from but one he believes is necessary to succeed.


We cover topics like:

•Why having a backup plan can be the riskiest decision of all. Harrison’s take on this will challenge the way you think about playing it “safe.”

item.title: Create A BLUEPRINT For Your DREAM LIFE With These 3 Steps— The Grateful Podcast 20
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

The Three Simple and Effective Steps to Chase your dreams and create your ultimate reality.

If you’re young and full of ambition, this episode is for you! I share my 3-step blueprint to achieving your biggest dreams during the crucial years of 18-25. Learn how to IMAGINE your dream life, CREATE actionable steps, and ADAPT to challenges along the way.

These three steps have been absolutely transformative in my own life. At 17, I was a high school senior with big dreams but no real roadmap to achieving them. I started small—imagining the kind of life I wanted to live, one that felt meaningful and exciting. I wanted to connect with others, explore the world, and build something impactful. This vision led me to start a tutoring business, FrenchFix, travel to France where I created lifelong connections, and even launch a podcast where I share the stories and strategies that inspire me.

The blueprint works because it’s flexible and personal. The creation phase helped me break my big dreams into small, actionable steps, like designing my first flyer for FrenchFix or setting aside time every day to write and plan content. And adapting? That’s where growth really happens—like when my YouTube videos didn’t take off immediately, so I shifted my focus, learned from feedback, and built an audience around topics that truly resonate.

This episode is not just about inspiration; it’s about giving you a framework to take control of your future. The ages of 18-25 are a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to build the foundation for a life that you love. Whether you’re unsure about what’s next or you’re already dreaming big, these steps will help you turn ambition into action and action into achievement.

💡 Don’t waste these transformative years—start building the life you deserve today. This episode will give you the tools and confidence to begin your journey.

🔔 Found value in this episode? Hit the like button, share it with a friend who needs to hear this, and subscribe for weekly content designed to help you unlock your potential. Send us Fan Mail

Slow Down to Speed Up: Stop Rushing and Live Intentionally 

The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner

Season 3 Episode 3


In this episode of The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner, we dive into the powerful concept of “Slow Down to Speed Up.” 🌿 Discover why rushing through life can leave you feeling burnt out and unfulfilled, and learn how intentional living can transform your personal and professional success.


I share practical tips to help you embrace mindfulness, prioritize what truly matters, and create space for meaningful growth. Whether you’re chasing a big dream, juggling daily responsibilities, or just looking to live with more purpose, this episode will inspire you to hit pause and realign with your goals.


✨ Key Takeaways:

✔️ Why slowing down can lead to faster progress

✔️ Simple strategies to live more intentionally

✔️ The mindset shift you need to overcome the pressure to “hustle”

item.title: Want to be A MAGNETIC SPEAKER? Start with THESE 7 HABITS — The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner 18
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

Let’s face it: bad communication skills can hold you back in every area of life—whether it’s your career, your relationships, or your ability to express yourself clearly.

You might think a pricey course is the solution, but what if it doesn’t work, leaving you with an empty wallet and the same problems?

Instead of taking that risk, wouldn’t you rather invest in proven habits that don’t cost a thing and can deliver lasting results?

If you don’t take action today, you could miss out on opportunities to connect, influence, and succeed—all because you didn’t take the time to improve how you communicate.

Are you thinking about buying a fancy communication course to improve your speaking skills?

Well, hold on, not so fast!

Before you make that VERY BIG investment, what if I told you there’s a natural, free way to become a master communicator without spending a single dime, just by implementing a few simple practices every day?

Today, we’re going to show you how.

In this video, we’ll explore seven daily habits that can help you master communication and build relationships like never before.

These methods are not only practical and effective but also things you can start doing today—without breaking the bank.

So, whether you’re a student, a professional, or simply someone who wants to connect better with others, you’re in the right place.

In just a few moments, we’ll dive into the psychology behind these habits and explain how they can transform your communication skills, answering key questions such as:
•“Why shouldn’t I spend hundreds of dollars on a communication course?”
•“What are the specific habits that can help me master communication?”
•“How do these habits work to improve my speaking, listening, and connection-building skills?”


Trying to just get more positive content on YouTube and the internet. I love my life and I hope the energy is contagious!

item.title: 17| Find Your Passion and Love Your Life With Annie Wagoner— The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

Today I have the privilege of releasing the first episode of The Grateful Podcast with a guest!

This special guest is my mom, Annie Wagoner.

Annie is one of the most amazing people I've ever met (I know I'm a bit biased but it's true). She walks into a room, and immediately, people start to smile. Her energy is contagious, and her love is admirable.

My mom created her business (Corenourishment) amidst the most stressful period of her life, and she wouldn't have done anything differently. Sometimes chaos births direction.

If you want to find your passion in life, learn how to feel joy, or just hear an amazing person speak about life, then listen here.

I am truly grateful to have my mom on The Grateful Podcast.


The Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner explores life’s challenges and joys, offering insights on personal growth, mental health, and cultivating gratitude. Through heartfelt stories and actionable advice, Jack inspires listeners to lead fulfilling and peaceful lives while embracing the power of kindness and self-reflection.

item.title: What comes first, being happy or being healthy? | The Grateful Pod. Ep. 12
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

Today, in episode 12, I try to answer a question that I had about the relationship between being healthy (turns into exercise) and happiness. I have seen contradictory data on the cause-and-effect relationship of the two and so this was my attempt at answering the question with you guys. 


If you wish to be loved, love. -Seneca

I feel love for all human kind, and that is really the type of message that I am trying to spread here.

Talking about spreading love my mom and I have started a challenge called the #spreadlove365challenge 

Participate in the #spreadlove365challenge ! 

https://www.instagram.com/spread_love.365?igsh=MjMwemNpdnZxcHZ5&utm_source=qr



Click the link below to support me on patreon! 

https://patreon.com/JackWagoner?utm_medium=clipboard_copy&utm_source=copyLink&utm_campaign=creatorshare_creator&utm_content=join_link

As I release this podcast I am over 7 months into a school year long exchange program in France. If you want to hear more about it check out some videos on my youtube channel where you can also watch the videos of the podcasts: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCL7rwtc5s_KcTZMHSJng-FQ




Study 1: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7369812/

Others:

item.title: See the intricacies in life and be present: Grateful Pod Ep.9
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

Presence. This is something that is so often talked about but I always hear something different. I believe presence is simple and it is one thing that nobody can ever take away from you.

In this episode I talk about how I have gone through my journey to feeling more present and give examples from books and spiritual leaders on presence as well. This one is not as science focused as it is really hard to genuinely measure presence. However, one thing I forgot to mention is that the worlds happiest man (measured brain activity) is a monk who is constantly focusing on his presence. 

PRESENCE IS HUGE.


If you wish to be loved, love. -Seneca

I feel love for all human kind, and that is really the type of message that I am trying to spread here.

item.title: All people want the same thing in life; Be open to stop division: Ep.7 Grateful Podcast
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

We are in a world of division. People despise other people for thinking differently. Why?

Dive into this episode of the Grateful podcast with Jack Wagoner to find out more of why and how we can fix it. Listen to his interesting take about how he believes every human wants the same thing in life, we just present it in a different manner.




If you wish to be loved, love. -Seneca

I feel love for all human kind, and that is really the type of message that I am trying to spread here.

Talking about spreading love my mom and I have started a challenge called the #spreadlove365challenge

item.title: The relationship between Joy and Accomplishment: Grateful Pod Ep.6
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

In today's episode Jack talks about the relationship between joy and accomplishing goals in life. Purpose is a big concept today. 

When you chase your purpose and every action has a reason, you find joy.

When you eat a snickers bar or play video games for 2 hours you might be feeling good in the moment, these are pleasures. That, is not happiness. Don’t chase it.


https://www.psychologytoday.com/us/basics/happiness/the-science-happiness

If you wish to be loved, love. -Seneca

I feel love for all human kind, and that is really the type of message that I am trying to spread here.

Talking about spreading love my mom and I have started a challenge called the #spreadlove365challenge 

Participate in the #spreadlove365challenge !

item.title: Become Comfortable Alone With Yourself, and Your Life Will Be Clear: Ep.3
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

In episode 3 of the Grateful Podcast with Jack Wagoner Jack goes into depth about the importance of becoming comfortable alone with yourself and your thoughts.

There were many studies mentioned in the episode today and the links will be available down below. I am going to release my notes for this podcast down below as well in which you will be able to see everything that I prepared for my episode as a way of holding me accountable and helping me get my true message across. 

There are so many instances where people just can't help but filling their time up but I am here to tell you that you should leave that time open in order to gain clarity and be happier, healthier, and be more GRATEFUL.

Do you know what ideas are actually yours?


Ok, welcome back to the Grateful podcast, as always I’m extremely grateful to be here recording, and working towards my dreams of making the world a happier, more grateful community. Today I’d like to start a tradition of starting each podcast with something I’m grateful for and this morning I am feeling really grateful for 


Today’s episode is going to be focusing on connecting to your inner dialogue, and genuinely understanding who you are. I believe that this is extremely important, actually I don’t know if I can explain in words how important I believe this is, especially with the amount of media and exterior input us humans receive daily. The quantity is insane. 



I was looking at this article by exploding topics, they track stats of just about anything with really accurate data, and saw that updated studies show that the average person in general spends 6 hours and 58 minutes per day staring at a screen. The average Gen Z kid, my generation, we spend an average of 9 HOURS on a screen per day. That is just crazy.


With all of this time preoccupied, doing something else, playing video games, scrolling on social media, how much time to we actually have to ourselves. I would like you to notice every time something stops during your day. Every slow moment, every time you are in a room with people you don’t know, or have a quick break. What do you do? If you are like most people you will pull out your phone. I do this too honestly pretty often, and it’s something I have really been trying to notice and work on. What these actions say to me is that I am not comfortable by myself, just with me, which is in my case not true so I should let myself be, without filling in all the gaps.

https://explodingtopics.com/blog/screen-time-stats


I want to start off by talking about a 2014 study published in the science magazine where  Timothy Wilson, a social psychologist at the University of Virginia in Charlottesville brought in hundreds of volunteers to a study where the volunteers would be given “think periods” ranging from 6 to 15 minutes. They were told to put away their belongings, most notably their cellphone, and were left alone with their thoughts for the time period assigned. Afterwards the participants had to rate the experience and over 50% said they did not enjoy it. The team of researchers took the experience a little further and added in a button in which the participant could shock themselves to get out of the experience. Beforehand every single participant said that they would have to be paid money in order to inflict a shock upon themselves, and yet 67% of men and 25% of women pushed that button. That is insane. People really cannot be alone with THEMSELVES for 15 minutes, that’s how uncomfortable they are with themselves. That’s how much they need exterior entertainment. Also, this was in 2014 and I don’t see any data saying that addiction to social media and other distractions has done anythin

item.title: Gratefulness and Accomplishing Your Goals: The Grateful Pod Ep.2
item.description:
Send us Fan Mail

In episode 2 of the Grateful Podcast, Jack talks about balancing your gratitude with striving for your goals and how the two values actually can have a symbiotic relationship. Jack uses examples from his life, quotes from philosophers new and old, and talks about some stoic philosophy as well.

Gratefulness is something that is often seen as settling for the life that you have right now, at least by people uneducated on what the topic really means. In this podcast Jack is here to tell you just how much of a lie that is. Gratefulness is the key to success, if there is such thing.

I hope you enjoyed the podcast and if you did please be sure to subscribe for more!

As I release this podcast episode I am over 4 and a half months into a school year long exchange program in France. If you want to hear more about it check out some other videos on my youtube channel. 

https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCL7rwtc5s_KcTZMHSJng-FQ 

My goal with this channel is to document my life growing up, and share my experiences and ideas with the world in a hope that some people can learn along with me. I love the idea of community, and hope to grow one here someday.

Click the link below to support me on patreon! 
https://patreon.com/JackWagoner?utm_medium=clipboard_copy&utm_source=copyLink&utm_campaign=creatorshare_creator&utm_content=join_link

Follow me on Instagram! 
https://www.instagram.com/jwago8?igsh=MXFpcHNyNmJ4aDNzMg%3D%3D&utm_source=qr

Thank you so much to everyone who watches my videos and listens to my podcasts, it means the world to me! When I make something that ultimately resonates with me, that’s the most important thing, but when it can also resonate with others it just makes it all that much better.
